 <p style="font-size:24pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="font-size:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-align:center">


<img src="g61756g78x51.jpg" alt="LOGO" style="width:1.9962in;height:0.412625in"/>
 </p> <p style="margin-top:24pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18.5pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Letter from the Board of Directors </p> <p style="margin-top:24pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">October&#160;21, 2026 </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9">Dear Shareholder, </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As directors, we are encouraged by Microsoft&#8217;s position at the forefront of the generational technology shift of artificial intelligence (&#8220;AI&#8221;) and proud of the Company&#8217;s progress in providing trusted AI infrastructure, platforms, and innovations that help individuals and organizations unlock new opportunities, improve productivity, and securely leverage their data and insights. Through disciplined governance, accountability, and a steadfast focus on security, quality, and long-term value creation, Microsoft remains well positioned to deliver sustainable growth for shareholders while advancing its mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Our fiscal year 2026 results demonstrate the strength of that strategy, with Microsoft delivering a record fiscal year and achieving revenue of $331.8&#160;billion and net income of $133.7&#160;billion. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">This Proxy Statement outlines Microsoft&#8217;s governance policies and practices that enable effective Board oversight of the Company&#8217;s strategy and operations. A core strength of our governance is the Board&#8217;s commitment to independent perspectives. Of the 12 Board nominees, 11 are independent, including Sandra Peterson as Lead Independent Director. Our nominees bring diverse backgrounds, experiences, and skills, which enhance the Board&#8217;s ability to manage risk and guide Microsoft for long-term success in a rapidly changing environment. In addition to subject matter expertise, we seek directors with proven leadership who can contribute meaningfully to oversight of the broad range of business, risk, and regulatory matters facing the Company. Since last year&#8217;s meeting, the Board appointed Carmine Di Sibio as a director in May 2026. He is standing for election by shareholders for the first time at the 2026 Annual Meeting. Mr.&#160;Di Sibio brings expertise in financial services, risk oversight, and global client leadership to meet the evolving needs of our customers. We are also pleased to announce the nomination of John Collison, <span style="white-space:nowrap">Co-founder,</span> President, and Director of Stripe Global Holdings, Inc., for election by shareholders at the 2026 Annual Meeting. Mr.&#160;Collison brings extensive entrepreneurial and operational experience, along with deep expertise in technology. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In addition, two members of the Board have decided not to seek <span style="white-space:nowrap">re-election</span> and will end their Board service in December: Reid Hoffman and Hugh Johnston. Mr.&#160;Hoffman served on the Board for nine years and on the Environmental, Social, and Public Policy Committee. During his nine-year tenure, Mr.&#160;Johnston served on and chaired the Audit and Finance Committee. We thank them for their many contributions. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Proxy Statement also includes information about all of the management and shareholder proposals up for a vote at the Company&#8217;s Annual Meeting. We value your input and encourage you to use one of the options laid out in this Proxy Statement to vote your shares whether or not you plan to join us for the Annual Meeting. For information on how Microsoft addresses topics of key importance to our shareholders and stakeholders, including cybersecurity, environmental sustainability, and responsible AI, we encourage you to read the progress reports on these topics that Microsoft published over the course of the past fiscal year which are available at <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/transparency</span> and <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/csr</span>. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As we look ahead, we continue to see tremendous opportunities for the Company&#8217;s business and shareholder value creation, with the ability to deliver positive impacts at a global scale. We appreciate your investment in Microsoft and thank you for the trust you place in us and the opportunity to serve you and our Company as directors. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Sincerely, </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Your Board of Directors </p> <p style="font-size:18pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top"/></tr>

<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Over 95% of the annual target compensation opportunity for our CEO is performance-based and over 50% for our other Named Executives</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Cash incentive awards are structured 50% (70% for CEO) based on <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-established</span> goals (balance of growth and profitability goals) and 50% (30% for CEO) based on operational performance as assessed across three performance categories, diversifying the risk associated with any single aspect of performance</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">The metrics for our performance stock awards are reviewed annually to ensure they reflect key business developments that drive long-term growth</p></div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Our performance stock awards (&#8220;PSAs&#8221;) include a relative total shareholder return (&#8220;TSR&#8221;) modifier to reward significant positive outperformance relative to the S&amp;P 500 and reduce rewards for underperformance to align executives&#8217; and shareholders&#8217; long-term interests</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">At least 80% of target compensation for our Named Executives was equity-based, with average across all Named Executives over 85%, providing incentives to drive long-term business success and direct alignment with returns to shareholders</p></div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Governance and Board Best Practices </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more is ambitious, and we cannot fulfill it with a narrow or short-term focus. Our adoption of leading governance practices fosters our sustained business success over the long term. Strong corporate governance, informed by participation from our shareholders, is essential to achieving our mission. The Lead Independent Director and Compensation Committee chair have ongoing consultations on governance and executive compensation topics with a cross-section of Microsoft&#8217;s large institutional investors. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Board believes that having a diverse mix of directors with complementary qualifications, expertise, and perspectives is essential to meeting its oversight responsibility. Of our 12 Board nominees, 11 are independent. Having an independent Board is a core element of our governance philosophy. <div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:25pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">1. Board of Directors and Governance </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft&#8217;s leadership in the artificial intelligence (&#8220;AI&#8221;) era depends not only on innovation, but also on earning and sustaining trust. As the Company develops and deploys technologies that are central to the way people and organizations work, communicate, and create, the Board believes that strong governance, effective oversight, and accountability are essential to long-term success. The Board remains focused on advancing Microsoft&#8217;s mission and strategic priorities in ways that sustain the trust placed in the Company by customers, partners, shareholders, and society. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft seeks to earn and maintain trust through responsible innovation, principled business practices, and transparency. As Microsoft develops and deploys technologies that increasingly shape how people and organizations work, communicate, and create, the Company remains committed to the responsible use of AI, protecting privacy, and advancing digital safety and cybersecurity. These commitments are supported by Microsoft&#8217;s longstanding culture of integrity and accountability, which is reflected in the Microsoft Standards of Business Conduct (our &#8220;Trust Code&#8221;), available at <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/policiesandguidelines</span>, and applies to our employees, executive officers, and members of the Board. We further strengthen accountability through comprehensive public reporting on our policies, practices, and performance, providing stakeholders visibility into how we are meeting our commitments and responsibilities. Our Reports Hub, available at <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/transparency</span>, offers a centralized view of reporting across a wide range of topics, including environmental sustainability, human rights, and political engagement. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_3"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Board of Directors Stewardship </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Shareholders elect our Board to serve their long-term interests and to oversee management. Our Board and its committees work closely with management to provide oversight, review, and counsel related to long-term strategy, risks and opportunities, and feedback from shareholders. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Strategy </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Led by our CEO, senior leadership develops and executes our business strategy. They manage our operations and work to model our desired culture, create innovative products, establish accountability, and control risk. Our CEO and senior leadership also align our structure, operations, people, policies, and compliance efforts to our mission, priorities, and culture. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">One of our Board&#8217;s primary responsibilities is overseeing management&#8217;s development and execution of the Company&#8217;s strategy. The Board works closely with senior leadership to respond to a dynamic business environment. Management benefits from the insights and perspectives of a diverse mix of directors with complementary qualifications, expertise, and attributes. Senior leadership and other leaders from across the Company provide business and strategy updates to our Board through regular strategy-focused meetings. At meetings throughout the year, the Board also assesses the strategic alignment of the Company&#8217;s budget and capital plan, business initiatives, and its strategic acquisition and integration process. For major initiatives, such as our approaches to security, quality, and reliability, the Board engages with management on strategic vision, investments, partnerships, capital requirements, and risks. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Risk&#160;Oversight </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Effective risk management is critical to Microsoft&#8217;s ability to achieve its mission. The Board exercises direct oversight of strategic risks to the Company and other risk areas not delegated to one of the Board&#8217;s committees. Our Board looks to the expertise of its committees to provide strategic oversight in their areas of focus. The committees are charged with specific areas of risk oversight and regularly report back to the full Board. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">The Board of Directors </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board oversees business affairs, integrity, risk management, CEO succession planning, and other matters reserved to the full Board and performs the annual CEO evaluation. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.56em; margin-right:1.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Oversees director selection and succession planning; Board effectiveness and independence, committee functions and charters; adherence to our corporate governance framework; and other corporate governance matters.</p></td></tr>
</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Company&#160;Management </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board, in consultation with each of its committees, oversees Company management in exercising its responsibility of managing risk. The Board relies upon senior leadership to supervise risk management activities within the Company. Senior leadership is responsible for developing a continuously improving culture of risk-aware practices to identify and manage the appropriate level of risk in pursuit of our business objectives. On a regular basis, the Board and its committees engage with our senior leadership, our chief risk executive and chief compliance officer, and other members of management on risk as part of broad strategic and operational discussions which encompass interrelated risks, as well as on a <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">risk-by-risk</span></span> basis. In addition, our integrated enterprise risk management approach is supported by operational management within business units, compliance and investigatory teams, enterprise and operational risk teams, internal audit and external audit reviews, and our legal department. Microsoft has also established robust standards of business conduct that apply to all employees globally and provides numerous methods for employees to elevate risk concerns directly to management or through anonymous channels. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:10pt;width:100%;border-spacing:0;margin:0 auto">


<tr>

<td style="width:33%"/>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom;width:1%"/>
<td style="width:33%"/>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom;text-align:center"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;text-align:center">Internal</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;text-align:center">Audit</p></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom;text-align:center"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;text-align:center">Integrated Enterprise</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;text-align:center">Risk Management</p></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom;text-align:center"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;text-align:center">Regulatory</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold;text-align:center">Governance</p></td></tr>

<td style="vertical-align:top">&#8195;</td></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt">
<td style="BORDER-RIGHT:0.75pt solid #999999;vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-right:1.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Provides independent and objective audit, investigative, and advisory services designed to provide assurance that the Company is appropriately addressing its risks; assists senior leadership and the Board in accomplishing their objectives by bringing a systematic, disciplined, technology-enabled approach to evaluate, investigate, and improve the effectiveness of risk management, governance, controls, and operations. AI tools and automation are embedded in the audit process to enhance visibility and accelerate reporting. The Audit and Finance Committee reviews the internal audit assessment quarterly.</p></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="BORDER-RIGHT:0.75pt solid #999999;vertical-align:top"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.56em; margin-right:1.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our integrated enterprise risk management approach establishes clear accountability and fosters collaboration across business units and compliance, audit, and legal functions. Senior leadership, with support of assigned risk owners, leads the identification, assessment, prioritization, and mitigation of the Company&#8217;s most significant risks with input from operational management, operational risk teams, and subject matter experts. The enterprise risk management team coordinates cross-company risk assessments and partners with internal audit to ensure focus on most significant risks. The Audit and Finance Committee reviews the enterprise risk management assessment semi-annually.</p> <p style="font-size:2pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt">&#160;</p></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.56em; margin-right:1.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">To comply with the accelerating global regulatory obligations, the Company has implemented comprehensive compliance programs across its operations to adapt to these changes and to maintain customer and regulator confidence. The Company monitors regulatory developments around the world and implements policies, controls, and technical safeguards so that its operations, products, services, and infrastructure meet applicable legal standards. The Company&#8217;s business teams, with legal support, manage the compliance programs and prepare external regulatory and commercial reporting, and the Company&#8217;s internal audit teams conduct reviews of the programs and processes.</p></td></tr>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_4"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Our Governance Structure </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Framework </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We have developed a corporate governance framework designed to ensure our Board has the practices in place to review and evaluate our business operations and to make decisions independent of management. Our goal is to align the interests of directors, management, and shareholders, and comply with or exceed the requirements of the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (&#8220;Nasdaq&#8221;) and applicable laws and regulations. This framework establishes the practices our Board follows with respect to, among other things, Board composition and member selection, Board meetings and involvement of senior leadership, director compensation, CEO performance evaluation, management succession planning, and Board committees. The Board is committed to seeking opportunities for improvements on an ongoing basis. Each summer, the Board reviews and, if appropriate, updates our corporate governance framework based on shareholder feedback, results from the annual shareholders meeting, the Board and committees&#8217; annual assessments, governance best practices, and regulatory developments. The documents listed below, and available on our website at <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/policiesandguidelines</span>, are maintained by the Company as part of our governance framework. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Shareholder Engagement </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Effective corporate governance includes regular, constructive conversations with our shareholders to proactively seek shareholder insights and to answer shareholder inquiries. We maintain an active dialogue with shareholders to ensure we thoughtfully consider a diversity of perspectives on issues including strategy, business performance, risk, culture and workplace topics, compensation practices, and a broad range of environmental and social topics. As noted above, the Board updates our corporate governance framework each summer based on a number of inputs, including shareholder feedback. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Office of the Corporate Secretary coordinates shareholder engagement with Investor Relations and provides a summary of all relevant environmental, social, and governance (&#8220;ESG&#8221;) feedback to our Board. In fiscal year 2026, we engaged on ESG topics with a cross-section of shareholders owning approximately 50% of Microsoft shares. The Lead Independent Director and Compensation Committee chair also have ongoing consultations on governance and executive compensation topics with a cross-section of Microsoft&#8217;s large institutional investors. In addition, throughout the year our Investor Relations group engages with our shareholders, frequently along with Satya Nadella, our Chairman and CEO, and Amy Hood, our CFO. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We also share relevant information through our Investor Relations website, our Annual Report, this Proxy Statement, our Reports Hub, and in posts on the Microsoft On the Issues blog. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Board Leadership </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board&#8217;s independent directors elected Satya Nadella to the role of Chairman and CEO, and Sandra&#160;Peterson as Lead Independent Director. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In his role, Mr.&#160;Nadella leverages his deep understanding of the business to elevate the right strategic opportunities and identify key risks and mitigation approaches for the Board&#8217;s review. As Lead Independent Director, Ms.&#160;Peterson has a clearly defined set of responsibilities, significant authority, and provides independent Board leadership. Key responsibilities and authority include: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Representing the Board with internal and external audiences, including shareholders </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board does not have a policy as to whether the Chairman should be an independent director, an affiliated director, or a member of management. The independent directors annually appoint a Chairman of the Board. To ensure robust independent leadership on the Board, if the individual appointed as Chairman is not an independent director, or when the independent directors determine that it is in the best interests of the Company, the independent directors will also annually appoint a Lead Independent Director. Our Board believes its current leadership structure is appropriate because it effectively allocates authority, responsibility, and oversight between management and the independent members of our Board. It does this by giving primary responsibility for the operational leadership and strategic direction of the Company to our Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, while enabling the Lead Independent Director to facilitate our Board&#8217;s independent oversight of management, promote communication between management and our Board, and support our Board&#8217;s consideration of key governance matters. The Board believes its programs for overseeing risk, as described in this Part 1 under &#8220;Risk Oversight,&#8221; would be effective under a variety of leadership frameworks and therefore do not materially affect its choice of structure. </p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">CEO Succession </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">A primary responsibility of the Board is planning for CEO succession and overseeing identification and development of other senior officers. The Board and the Compensation Committee work with the CEO and our Chief Human Resources Officer to plan for succession. For the CEO, the succession plan covers identification of internal and external candidates, and professional and leadership development plans for internal candidates. The Board annually reviews the CEO succession plan. The criteria used to assess potential CEO candidates are formulated based on the Company&#8217;s business strategies, and include strategic vision, leadership, and operational execution. The Board is committed to actively seeking highly qualified women and individuals from minority groups to include in the pool of potential CEO candidates. The Board maintains an emergency succession contingency plan that is reviewed on an annual basis by the Board and Governance and Nominating Committee. The plan identifies roles and responsibilities of individuals who would act if an unforeseen event prevented the CEO from continuing to serve. The Compensation Committee reviews the plan with the CEO and reports to the Board on development and succession plans for the other senior officers. The Board may review development and succession planning more frequently as it deems necessary or desirable. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Annual Board and Committee Evaluation Process </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board is committed to a rigorous self-evaluation process. The Governance and Nominating Committee annually evaluates the performance of the Board. In fiscal year 2026, the evaluation included utilizing a third-party facilitator to seek feedback from each director on the performance of the Board and each committee. The results were reported to and discussed with the Board and each relevant committee. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our evaluation process is designed to elicit feedback on the processes, structure, composition, and effectiveness of the Board and each committee. The evaluation results have facilitated increased Board and committee effectiveness, including driving clarity on key areas for the Board&#8217;s focus over the coming year, focus on sustainable growth strategies for the Company, and input on management development and succession planning, as well as Board and committee composition and recruiting. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Director Attendance </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Each quarter, our Board holds <span style="white-space:nowrap">two-day</span> meetings comprised of committee and Board meetings. At each quarterly Board meeting, time is set aside for the independent directors to meet without management present. Additional executive sessions are held as needed. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In addition to the quarterly meetings, typically there are other regularly scheduled Board and committee meetings and several special meetings each year. Our Board met nine times during fiscal year 2026. In addition, the Board held periodic strategy sessions, which included presentations and discussions with senior officers and other senior leadership. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Each director nominee attended at least 75% of the aggregate of all fiscal year 2026 meetings of the Board and each committee on which he or she served. In fiscal year 2026, the Board and committees of the Board held a total of 33 meetings. Together, the director nominees attended at least 90% of the combined total meetings of the Board and the committees on which they were members in fiscal year 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Directors are expected to attend the annual shareholders meeting, if practicable. All directors attended the 2025 Annual Meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Director Orientation and Continuing Education </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our orientation programs are designed to familiarize new directors with our businesses, strategies, and policies and assist new directors in developing Company and industry knowledge to optimize their service on the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We support our directors in their continuing education by providing programs that enhance the skills and knowledge directors use to perform their responsibilities. These programs may include internally developed programs or programs presented by third parties. Past sessions covered topics ranging from Microsoft&#8217;s evolving marketing and brand strategy to <span style="white-space:nowrap">hands-on</span> experiences with the Gaming and XBOX roadmap and the Company&#8217;s vision for Microsoft AI. </p>

<td style="vertical-align:top"> <div style="font-size: 4pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; margin-left: 0.86em; font-size: 7pt; font-family: Arial; line-height: normal;">AUDIT AND<br/> FINANCE&#160;COMMITTEE<br/> MATTERS</div> </td>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"> <div style="font-size: 4pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; margin-left: 0.86em; font-size: 7pt; font-family: Arial; line-height: normal;">PROPOSALS&#160;TO<br/> BE&#160;VOTED&#160;ON&#160;DURING&#8195;&#8195;<br/> THE MEETING</div> </td>

<td style="vertical-align:top"> <div style="font-size: 4pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; margin-left: 0.86em; font-size: 7pt; font-family: Arial; line-height: normal;">INFORMATION&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;<br/> ABOUT THE<br/> MEETING</div> </td> </tr>
<tr style="font-size:1px">

<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> <div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%"> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Director Stock Ownership Policy </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">To align the interests of our directors and shareholders, our directors are required to own Microsoft shares equal in value to at least three times the base annual retainer (cash and stock) payable to a director. Each director must retain 50% of all net shares <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">(post-tax)</div> from the retainer until reaching the minimum share ownership requirement. Stock deferred under the Deferred Compensation Plan for <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Non-Employee</div> Directors counts toward the minimum ownership requirement. Each of our directors complied with our stock ownership policy in fiscal year 2026. </div> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Derivatives Trading, Hedging, and Pledging </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our directors and executive officers are prohibited from trading in options, puts, calls, or other derivative instruments related to Microsoft equity or debt securities. They also are prohibited from purchasing Microsoft common stock on margin, borrowing against Microsoft common stock held in a margin account, or pledging Microsoft common stock as collateral for a loan. Employees, other than executive officers, are generally permitted to engage in transactions designed to hedge or offset market risk. </div> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Insider Trading Policies and Procedures </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We have <ix:nonNumeric name="ecd:InsiderTrdPoliciesProcAdoptedFlag" contextRef="P07_01_2025To06_30_2026" format="ixt:fixed-true" id="ixv-25965">adopted</ix:nonNumeric> insider trading policies and procedures applicable to our directors, officers, and employees, and have implemented processes for the Company that we believe are reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws, rules, and regulations, and the Nasdaq listing standards. Our General Insider Trading Policy prohibits our employees and related persons and entities from trading in securities of Microsoft and other companies while in possession of material, nonpublic information. Our General Insider Trading Policy also prohibits our employees from disclosing material, nonpublic information of Microsoft, or another publicly traded company, to others who may trade on the basis of that information. Our Restricted Trading Window Policy requires that certain officers of the Company (corporate vice presidents and above) and other designated employees only transact in Microsoft securities during an open window period, subject to limited exceptions. In addition, certain officers of the Company are required to obtain approval in advance of transactions in Microsoft securities. Our executive officers and directors must also comply with additional trading restrictions. The foregoing summary of our insider trading policies and procedures does not purport to be complete and is qualified by reference to our General Insider Trading Policy, Restricted Trading Window Policy, and Insider Trading Compliance and Preclearance Policies for Section&#160;16 Officers and Directors of Microsoft, copies of which can be found as exhibits to our Annual Report on Form <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">10-K</div> for the fiscal year ended June&#160;30, 2026. </div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Board Independence </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board&#8217;s independence enables it to be objective and critical in carrying out its oversight responsibilities. The Corporate Governance Guidelines provide that a substantial majority of our directors will be independent. The independent members of the Board annually appoint a Lead Independent Director to facilitate the Board&#8217;s oversight of management, promote communication between management and our Board, engage with shareholders, and lead consideration of key governance matters. Key elements of our Board independence include: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">11 of 12 director nominees are independent</span>. We are committed to maintaining a substantial majority of directors who are independent of the Company and management. Except for our Chairman and CEO, Satya Nadella, all director nominees are independent </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">Board tenure</span>. We are committed to board refreshment. To strike a balance between retaining directors with deep knowledge of the Company and adding directors with a fresh perspective, the Board seeks to maintain an average tenure of 10 years or less for its independent directors as a group. The average tenure for our independent director nominees is 6.7 years. The average tenure is 6.8 years if Mr.&#160;Nadella is included </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

The Board is committed to actively seeking highly qualified women and individuals from minority groups to include in the pool of potential Board nominees and CEO candidates </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

At each quarterly Board meeting, time is set aside for the independent directors to meet in executive session without management present. Additional executive sessions are held as needed </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

Only independent directors are members of the Board&#8217;s committees. Each committee meets regularly in executive session </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

The compensation consultant retained by the Compensation Committee is independent of the Company and management as required by the Compensation Consultant Independence Standards </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

As described in the &#8220;Board Leadership&#8221; section, the Lead Independent Director has a clearly defined set of responsibilities, significant authority, and provides independent Board leadership </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Board Committees </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">To support effective corporate governance, our Board delegates certain responsibilities to its committees, who report on their activities to the Board. These committees have the authority to engage legal counsel or other advisors or consultants as they deem appropriate to carry out their responsibilities. Our Board has four standing committees: an Audit and Finance Committee, a Compensation Committee, an Environmental, Social, and Public Policy Committee, and a Governance and Nominating Committee. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As provided in our Corporate Governance Guidelines, members of the Audit and Finance Committee ordinarily may not serve on over three public company audit committees (including Microsoft&#8217;s). In calculating service on a public company board or audit committee, service on a board or audit committee of a parent and its substantially-owned subsidiary counts as service on a single board or audit committee. Any Audit and Finance Committee member&#8217;s service on over three public company audit committees will be subject to the Board&#8217;s determination that the member is able to effectively serve on the Company&#8217;s Audit and Finance Committee. The Governance and Nominating Committee and the Board considered Ms.&#160;List&#8217;s service on four public company audit committees, including her professional qualifications, former experience as a public company chief financial officer, the fact she is retired from active employment, and the nature of and time involved in her service on other boards. Following such review, the Board determined that Ms.&#160;List is able to effectively continue to serve on the Company&#8217;s Audit and Finance Committee. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Compensation&#160;Committee </span></span></p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

The Committee may delegate to one or more executive officers the authority to make grants of equity-based compensation to eligible individuals who are not executive officers and to administer the Company&#8217;s equity-based compensation plans. The Committee has delegated to senior leadership the authority to make stock award grants to employees who are not Section&#160;16 officers and to administer the Company&#8217;s equity-based compensation plans. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Independent compensation consultant</span>. The Compensation Committee retained Pay Governance LLC as its independent compensation consultant throughout fiscal year 2026. The consultant advises the Committee on marketplace trends in executive compensation, management proposals for compensation programs, and executive officer compensation decisions. The consultant also evaluates compensation for <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</span> directors, other members of senior leadership, and equity compensation programs generally. The consultant discusses recommendations to the Board on CEO compensation with the Committee and is directly accountable to the Committee. To maintain the independence of the consultant&#8217;s advice, the firm does not provide services to Microsoft other than those described above. The Committee has adopted Compensation Consultant Independence Standards, which can be viewed on our website at <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/policiesandguidelines</span>. These standards require that the Committee annually assess the independence of its compensation consultant. A consultant satisfying the following requirements will be considered independent. The Committee will report to the full Board on the conclusions of any investigation that results in a founded determination and the disciplinary and other actions taken </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="font-size:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_5"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Director Selection and Qualifications </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Shareholders elect our Board of Directors annually. In making its annual director nominations determination, the Board&#8217;s objective is to recommend a group of directors that can best ensure the continuing success of our business and represent shareholder interests through the exercise of sound judgment using its diversity of experience and perspectives. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Governance and Nominating Committee recommends to the Board director candidates for nomination and election during the annual shareholders meeting or for appointment to fill vacancies. The Committee works with our Board to strategically consider the composition and skills needed on the Board over the short-, medium-, and long-term. In doing so, they determine the characteristics, skills, and experience for the Board as a whole and its individual members with the objective of having a board with diverse backgrounds, skills, and experience. In making its recommendations to our Board, the Committee considers the qualifications of individual director candidates applying the Board membership criteria described below. The Committee retains any search firm involved in identifying potential candidates and approves their fees. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">For all directors, we require an independent mindset, integrity, personal and professional ethics, business judgment, and the ability and willingness to commit sufficient time to the Board. Our Board considers many factors in evaluating the suitability of individual </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">How to Communicate with our Board </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We will transmit shareholder communications related to corporate governance and other Board matters to the Board, a committee of the Board, or a director as designated in your message. </table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Concerns about accounting or auditing matters or possible violations of our Standards of Business Conduct should be reported under the procedures outlined in the Microsoft Standards of Business Conduct, which is available on our Microsoft integrity website at <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/legal/compliance/integrity</span>. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Director Independence </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Board has adopted director independence guidelines to assist in determining each director&#8217;s independence. These guidelines are available on our website at <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/policiesandguidelines</span>. The guidelines either meet or are more restrictive than the definition of &#8220;independent director&#8221; in the listing requirements of Nasdaq and applicable laws and regulations. The guidelines identify categories of relationships the Board has determined would not affect a director&#8217;s independence and therefore are not considered by the Board in determining director independence. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Following the director independence guidelines, each year and before a new director is appointed, the Board must affirmatively determine a director has no relationship that would interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out their responsibilities as a director. Annually, each director completes a detailed questionnaire that provides information about relationships that might affect the determination of independence. Management provides the Governance and Nominating Committee and Board with relevant known facts and circumstances of any relationship bearing on the independence of a director or nominee that is outside the categories permitted under the director independence guidelines. The Committee then completes an assessment of each director considering all known relevant facts and circumstances concerning any relationship bearing on the independence of a director or nominee. This process includes evaluating whether any identified relationship otherwise adversely affects a director&#8217;s independence and affirmatively determining that the director has no material relationship with Microsoft, another director, or as a partner, shareholder, or officer of an organization that has a relationship with our Company. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Governance and Nominating Committee also considers the tenure of a director, and for longer serving directors, whether the duration of service impacts the director&#8217;s independence from management, as demonstrated by the director&#8217;s relationship with management and the director&#8217;s participation in Board and committee deliberations. The Board seeks to maintain an average tenure of 10 years or less for its independent directors as a group. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Based on the review and recommendation by the Governance and Nominating Committee, the Board analyzed the independence of each director and nominee. The Board determined that Mses. List, MacGregor, Peterson, Pritzker, and Walmsley, and Messrs. Collison, Di Sibio, Hoffman, Johnston, Mason, Rainey, Scharf, and Stanton (as well as Carlos Rodriguez, whose Board service ended on December&#160;5, 2025) meet the standards of independence under our Corporate Governance Guidelines, the director independence guidelines, and applicable Nasdaq listing standards, including that each member is free of any relationship that would interfere with his or her individual exercise of independent judgment. In making its independence determination, the Committee and Board considered ordinary course transactions between Microsoft and certain related entities, for instance the purchase of software licenses by companies of which a director is an executive officer, and purchases by Microsoft of goods and services from such companies. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Certain Relationships and Related Transactions </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We are a global company with extensive operations in the U.S. and many foreign countries. Every year, we spend billions of dollars for goods and services purchased from third parties. The authority of our employees to purchase goods and services is widely dispersed. Because of these wide-ranging activities, there may be transactions, business arrangements, or relationships with businesses and other organizations in which one of our directors, executive officers, nominees for director, or an owner of 5% or more of our stock (&#8220;5% shareholders&#8221;), or their immediate families, may also be a director, executive officer, or investor, or have </p>

We will refer to these transactions with related entities as related-party transactions where the amount involved exceeds $120,000 and a director, executive officer, nominee for director or 5% shareholders, or immediate family member has a direct or indirect material interest. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Related-party transactions have the potential to create actual or perceived conflicts of interest between Microsoft and its directors, executive officers, nominees for director or 5% shareholders, or their immediate family members. The Audit and Finance Committee has established a written policy and procedures for review and approval of related-party transactions. If a related-party transaction subject to review involves directly or indirectly a member of the Audit and Finance Committee (or an immediate family member or domestic partner), the remaining Committee members will conduct the review. In evaluating a related-party transaction, the Audit and Finance Committee considers, among other factors: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

The Audit and Finance Committee also requires that the transaction meet the same Microsoft standards that apply to comparable transactions with unaffiliated entities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">During fiscal year 2026, there were ordinary course transactions between Microsoft and certain related entities, for instance the purchase of software licenses by companies of which a director is an executive officer and purchases by Microsoft of goods and services from such companies. None of these transactions constituted a related-party transaction that required approval by the Audit and Finance Committee. </p>

<div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_8"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Director Compensation </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Compensation Committee periodically reviews the regular annual retainer paid to <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</span> directors and makes recommendations for adjustments, as appropriate, to the full Board. Our objective for compensation to <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</span> directors is to award the majority of compensation in equity to further align the interests of our Board with those of our shareholders and to make meaningful adjustments every few years, rather than smaller adjustments that are more frequent. There was no change for fiscal year 2026. Our CEO, Mr.&#160;Nadella does not receive pay for serving as a director or as Board Chairman. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Company reimburses reasonable expenses incurred for Board-related activities. Directors may participate in our corporate matching gift program for charitable donations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Director retainers are paid quarterly in arrears. Quarterly periods are measured beginning with the annual shareholders meeting. For the first quarterly period following the annual shareholders meeting, we pay 25% of the total annual retainer to each director on the last trading day in January. For the remaining quarterly periods, we pay 25% of the total annual retainer to each director at the end of the quarterly period. The number of shares awarded each quarterly period is determined by dividing the dollar value of the stock award by the market price of our common stock as of the last business day of the period. Retainers are <span style="white-space:nowrap">pro-rated</span> for directors who join or leave the Board or have a change in Board role during a quarterly period. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Directors may elect to defer and convert to deferred stock awards all or part of their annual cash retainer, and to defer receipt of all or part of their annual stock awards retainer under the Deferred Compensation Plan for <span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</span> Directors. Amounts deferred are maintained in bookkeeping accounts that are deemed invested in Microsoft common stock, and dividends paid on deemed investments are also deemed to be invested in our common stock. We calculate the number of shares credited by dividing the amount deferred by the closing market price of our common stock on the originally scheduled payment date. Accounts in the plan are distributed in shares of Microsoft common stock, with payments either in installments beginning on separation from Board service or in a lump sum paid no later than the fifth anniversary after separation from Board service. </p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:25pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc61756_9">2.&#160;Named&#160;Executive&#160;Officer&#160;Compensation </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_10"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">A Letter from the Compensation Committee </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Dear Shareholder, </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The pace of technological change continues to increase, but the underpinnings of our executive compensation program remain constant.&#160;We tie Microsoft&#8217;s long-term strategic goals with shareholder interests while offering a competitive total rewards package to attract, motivate, and retain the key executives who drive our business and develop the next generation of Microsoft leaders. We remain committed to ongoing evaluation of our compensation program to preserve that alignment. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our fiscal year 2026 results, which include achieving revenue of $331.8&#160;billion and net income of $133.7&#160;billion, continue Microsoft&#8217;s longstanding track record of growth in both revenue and profit under Satya Nadella&#8217;s tenure.&#160;He&#160;and his leadership team have positioned Microsoft as a clear leader in the ongoing generational technology shift and at the forefront of AI advancement, enabling Microsoft to drive long-term growth through security, quality, and innovation. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In fiscal year 2026, Microsoft achieved 18% revenue growth and a 21% increase in operating income. This impressive performance resulted in a 129.03% payout as a percentage of target on the financial metric-based portion of our annual cash incentives and a 117.09% payout as a percentage of target on the performance stock award core strategic metrics, demonstrating clear alignment between compensation outcomes and our&#8201;pay-for-performance&#8201;philosophy. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">During the past fiscal year, Microsoft continued its robust shareholder outreach, engaging with investors representing approximately 50% of outstanding shares. Among those engagements, the Board&#8217;s Lead Independent Director and Compensation Committee chair discussed governance and executive compensation with a cross-section of large institutional investors. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Committee is gratified that the views of most Microsoft shareholders are consistent with the Committee&#8217;s own perspective: Mr.&#8201;Nadella should be compensated in ways that encourage his continued leadership and drive sustained business growth and shareholder value. In accordance with this view, Mr. Nadella&#8217;s equity compensation is delivered exclusively through performance stock awards tied to long-term value creation and does not include any time-based equity awards. Including his annual cash incentive, more than 95% of Mr. Nadella&#8217;s annual total target compensation opportunity was performance-based. For fiscal year 2026, we set Mr. Nadella&#8217;s target performance stock award at $50 million, a level unchanged since fiscal year 2022. We determined that this level appropriately reflected Mr. Nadella&#8217;s exceptional leadership, the scope of his responsibilities, and the scale, complexity, and performance of Microsoft. This target value appears in the compensation tables at a higher value primarily due to the required accounting model for reporting purposes. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Consistent with prior years, Mr. Nadella&#8217;s fiscal year 2026 annual cash incentive was weighted 70% toward financial performance and 30% toward operational performance. In fiscal year 2026, Microsoft&#8217;s strong financial results led to a 129.03% payout as a percentage of target, while the Board assessed Mr. Nadella&#8217;s operational performance at 156.67% payout as a percentage of target, based on his contributions across the three categories described on page 43 below. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Each year the Committee reviews the compensation program outlined in the following pages to ensure it advances our <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">pay-for-performance</span></span> philosophy. We welcome your feedback and perspectives on how we are doing. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Thank you for your continued trust and investment in Microsoft. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Sincerely, </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">The Compensation Committee </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Catherine MacGregor (Chair) </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Carmine Di Sibio </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Sandra E. Peterson </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Charles W.  <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft&#8217;s executive compensation program is designed by our Compensation Committee and Board of Directors to align to Microsoft&#8217;s long-term strategy.  </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Continued Innovation and Growth </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Since his appointment as Chief Executive Officer in 2014, Satya Nadella has led the<span style="font-style:italic"> </span>Company&#8217;s mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Under his leadership, Microsoft has strengthened its strategic position by helping customers navigate profound technological change and accelerating innovation across the Company. Mr.&#160;Nadella&#8217;s tenure has been marked by exceptional, sustained financial performance. Over 12 years, Microsoft nearly quadrupled revenue from $86.8&#160;billion to $331.8&#160;billion, increased net income more than sixfold from $22.1&#160;billion to $133.7&#160;billion, and expanded diluted earnings per share nearly sevenfold from $2.63 to $17.95, delivering annual compounded growth across these three metrics of 11.8%, 16.2%, and 17.4%, respectively. This sustained operating performance has contributed to significant value creation for long-term shareholders. Microsoft has transformed its culture, strengthened its commitment to innovation and customer success, and developed a broad technology ecosystem that uniquely connects cloud, security, productivity software, and artificial intelligence (&#8220;AI&#8221;). The examples below illustrate how Mr.&#160;Nadella&#8217;s strategic priorities and disciplined execution have translated into durable competitive advantages, expanded Microsoft&#8217;s addressable market, strengthened customer relationships, and delivered measurable business outcomes. </p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Security and Trust.</span> Mr.&#160;Nadella and our senior leaders prioritized continued innovation at the intersection of AI, security, privacy, and compliance. As cyber threats have grown in scale and sophistication, security has remained a core priority across Microsoft&#8217;s products, platforms, and operations, including through the Secure Future Initiative. Microsoft serves approximately 1.6&#160;million security customers, with more than one million customers using four or more Microsoft security workloads, demonstrating customers&#8217; increasing reliance on Microsoft as a strategic security provider and validating the Company&#8217;s integrated platform approach. Drawing on signals across the Microsoft ecosystem, the Company is using AI to both strengthen customers&#8217; security postures and help secure their AI deployments. During fiscal year 2026, Microsoft introduced Project Perception, a multi-model agentic security system designed to simulate attacks, investigate threats, and accelerate remediation, and security triage agents handles millions of alerts, helping automate high-volume security workflows and improving the speed and scale at which customers can detect and respond to threats. Microsoft is also enabling customers to adopt AI with confidence through Microsoft Purview, which provides robust tools for data security, data governance, and data compliance and has audited more than 50&#160;billion Copilot interactions to support customers&#8217; compliance obligations. These capabilities reinforce Microsoft&#8217;s position as a trusted technology provider and support customer adoption of AI by addressing security, compliance, and governance requirements that are critical to enterprise deployment at scale. Microsoft also provides consumers with robust protections including through the Microsoft privacy dashboard, which has an average of 2.7&#160;million monthly users, demonstrating active engagement and global use. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Platform and Infrastructure.</span> Microsoft&#8217;s cloud and AI infrastructure development reflect Microsoft&#8217;s long-term strategic choice to build the platform capacity required for enterprise AI adoption through the construction of one of the world&#8217;s largest and most sophisticated technology platforms. To support that increasing customer demand, Microsoft has continued to aggressively expand its global infrastructure footprint, adding 88 datacenters during the fiscal year, including 31 in the fourth quarter alone, while improving deployment efficiency and accelerating the availability of new computing resources. This expansion increased Microsoft&#8217;s capacity to serve cloud and AI demand and accelerated the pace at which new capacity became available for customer use. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft&#8217;s platform differentiation extends beyond scale. Mr.&#160;Nadella and our senior leaders have focused the Company on continuous innovation across silicon, systems, software, sovereignty, and model choice to improve performance, flexibility, and efficiency for customers. This full-stack approach helps Microsoft manage supply constraints, optimize workload performance, and give customers more deployment options. Microsoft has also invested in proprietary technologies, including Maia 200 and Cobalt 200, alongside the latest offerings from NVIDIA and AMD, creating a diverse and optimized foundation for AI workloads. These investments, combined with ongoing software and infrastructure optimization, improved inference throughput by 40% for Microsoft&#8217;s most-used AI models and increased throughput for Copilot workloads fourfold, enhancing the Company&#8217;s ability to scale AI services efficiently as customer adoption continues to accelerate. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Beyond infrastructure, Microsoft is building the enterprise AI stack required for customers to deploy AI responsibly and at scale. Fabric surpassed 40,000 paid customers enabling them to connect agents to real-time operational, analytical, and unstructured data, while Foundry reached 100,000 customers and more than doubled revenue year-over-year. Foundry provides customers with access to more than 11,000 models, including offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, xAI, and Microsoft&#8217;s own MAI family. This breadth of model choice enables customers to select solutions based on quality, latency, cost, sovereignty, and compliance requirements, while reinforcing Microsoft&#8217;s position as an open and flexible enterprise AI platform. Together with Agent 365, which is helping tens of thousands of companies manage tens of millions of agents, and Microsoft&#8217;s broader governance capabilities, these platforms help customers integrate AI into business processes while retaining control of their data, workflows, and intellectual property. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The combination of infrastructure, model choice, governance, and agent management creates a differentiated enterprise AI ecosystem designed to support customer adoption across a broad range of workloads and deployment requirements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Applications and Agents.</span> Mr.&#160;Nadella and our senior leaders have focused Microsoft on delivering applications and agentic systems that help customers improve productivity, accelerate innovation, and achieve measurable business outcomes. Through Microsoft 365, Microsoft is helping customers work more effectively, collaborate more seamlessly, and realize greater value from their technology investments. With more than 450&#160;million paid commercial seats and growing adoption of premium offerings, Microsoft continues to embed these innovations into customers&#8217; daily workflows. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption continued to accelerate during fiscal year 2026, surpassing 30&#160;million paid seats. The scale of adoption reflects growing customer confidence in Microsoft&#8217;s ability to deliver enterprise-ready AI capabilities integrated directly into existing workflows. Microsoft also delivered 625 Copilot updates during the year, reflecting its rapid pace of innovation and commitment to customer feedback. Customer engagement and satisfaction increased as Microsoft enhanced performance and expanded capabilities. Large-scale enterprise deployments accelerated across industries, with the number of customers deploying Copilot broadly across their organizations continuing to increase as Copilot evolved from an AI assistant into a platform for agentic work. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>
