 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft&#8217;s application-layer innovation extends beyond Microsoft 365 Copilot. GitHub now has 225&#160;million users, with 50&#160;million using Copilot, and one in three pull requests involving an agent. Microsoft also expanded industry-specific AI offerings, including Dragon Copilot for healthcare, which is being used by over 100,000 healthcare providers to help automate administrative and clinical workflows. Together, these examples demonstrate Microsoft&#8217;s ability to translate platform investments into widely adopted applications that improve customer productivity, accelerate software development, and create new opportunities for long-term growth. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Advertising, LinkedIn, and XBOX. </span>Microsoft&#8217;s consumer-facing businesses further demonstrate the Company&#8217;s ability to pair technological innovation with broad global reach. In Search advertising, Bing and Edge have gained share for five consecutive years. Bing reached one billion monthly active users for the first time during fiscal year 2026, while Edge continued its sustained market share gains. Search advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 10% in the fourth quarter, driven by higher revenue per search and search volume. Microsoft also continues investing in Windows as a leading platform for secure edge AI. Windows powers more than 1.6&#160;billion active devices worldwide, combining powerful <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-device</span> computing with enterprise-grade security to help customers benefit from AI wherever work occurs. LinkedIn remains an important component of Microsoft&#8217;s ecosystem and continued to generate strong engagement, achieving double-digit member growth for the fifth consecutive year. With over 1.3&#160;billion members worldwide, LinkedIn is one of the world&#8217;s largest professional networks and recruiters at more than 20,000 companies now use Microsoft&#8217;s <span style="white-space:nowrap">AI-powered</span> hiring solutions. In XBOX, Microsoft is taking the actions required across its content portfolio, platform, and operations to reset the business for long-term growth. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Corporate Leadership </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Taken together, these accomplishments reflect Mr.&#160;Nadella&#8217;s guidance through a period of extraordinary technological change. By fostering a culture centered on innovation, learning, accountability, and customer success, Mr.&#160;Nadella has helped Microsoft anticipate major platform shifts, allocate capital toward long-term opportunities, and execute across infrastructure, platforms, applications, and consumer experiences. At the same time, Microsoft&#8217;s efforts to advance technology and support customers are guided by our broader responsibilities to society. As AI becomes increasingly central to the global economy, Microsoft&#8217;s leadership has focused not only on advancing AI innovation, but also on helping ensure AI is developed and deployed responsibly, securely, and in a manner that protects privacy and fundamental rights. Consistent with its mission, Microsoft seeks to expand opportunity, earn trust, and advance sustainability through the products and services it provides. We provide extensive public reporting on these matters at <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/trust-center</span> and <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/transparency</span>. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_13"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Section&#160;2 &#8211; Executive Compensation Program </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Executive Compensation Philosophy </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We design our executive compensation program to attract, motivate, and retain the key executives who drive our success and industry leadership while considering Company and individual performance and alignment with the long-term interests of our shareholders. We achieve our objectives through a compensation program that: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Maintain a robust stock ownership policy that reinforces the alignment of executive officer and shareholder interests (including requiring stock ownership of 15x base salary for our&#160;CEO)</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Have an executive compensation recovery (&#8220;clawback&#8221;) policy&#160;that allows for recoupment in the event of a restatement or misconduct to ensure accountability</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Promote long-term focus through multi-year vesting and performance requirements</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Use a combination of absolute and relative performance measures</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Prohibit pledging, hedging, and trading in derivatives of Microsoft securities</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; Feedback received from our shareholders through ongoing engagement discussions informs our Compensation Committee&#8217;s deliberations as it reviews the incentive structures&#160;in&#160;place on an ongoing basis. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Board and our Compensation Committee deeply value the continued interest of and feedback from our shareholders on our executive compensation&#160;program&#160;and are committed to maintaining an active dialogue with them to ensure their perspectives are thoughtfully taken into account. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We carefully consider both the level of voting support from our <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">shareholders&#160;on&#160;our&#160;say-on-pay</span></span> vote, as well as comments from shareholders,&#160;when evaluating our executive compensation program. At the 2025 Annual Meeting, over 91% of the votes cast supported our advisory resolution on the compensation of our Named Executives <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">(&#8220;say-on-pay&#8221;</span></span> vote). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As in prior years, in fiscal year 2026 we continued our active shareholder engagement program, discussing compensation and a broad range of environmental, social, and governance issues with shareholders representing approximately 50% of our outstanding shares. The Lead Independent Director and Compensation Committee chair also have ongoing consultations on governance and executive compensation topics with a cross-section of Microsoft&#8217;s large institutional investors, and in fiscal year 2026, participated in meetings with shareholders representing almost 30% of outstanding shares. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In evaluating our compensation practices in fiscal year 2026, our Compensation Committee was mindful of the support our shareholders expressed for our philosophy and practice of linking executive compensation to operational objectives and shareholder value creation and did not make any substantial changes to our executive compensation program. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_14"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Section&#160;3 &#8211; Pay Setting Governance and Process </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Compensation Committee establishes the design of our executive compensation program. After considering Mr.&#160;Nadella&#8217;s recommendations, our Compensation Committee also approves the annual target compensation (base salaries, target cash incentives, and equity incentive compensation) for our Named Executives, except Mr.&#160;Nadella. After considering the recommendation of our Compensation Committee, the independent members of our Board approved Mr.&#160;Nadella&#8217;s base salary, target cash incentive, and target performance stock award (&#8220;PSA&#8221;), providing no time-based stock awards for fiscal year 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Compensation Committee also retains, and seeks the advice of, Pay Governance, an executive compensation consulting firm that is independent of management. See Part 1 &#8211; Board of Directors and Governance &#8211; Board Committees for more information on Pay Governance&#8217;s role and independence as an advisor to the Compensation Committee. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Competitive Pay </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Attracting, retaining, and motivating exceptional executive talent is critical to our long-term success. We compete for leaders in a dynamic and competitive market where organizations are increasingly seeking executives who can lead through technological disruption, capitalize on <span style="white-space:nowrap">AI-driven</span> opportunities, and manage complex global businesses. Competition for these individuals is significant and increasing, and compensation levels reflect this demand. We expect these conditions to persist and will continue to evaluate our executive compensation programs to ensure they support the recruitment, retention, and motivation of the leaders necessary to execute our strategy. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Approach to Compensation Benchmarking </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">To ensure that our Board and Compensation Committee have current information to set appropriate compensation levels, we conduct an executive compensation market analysis each year that draws from third-party compensation surveys and publicly available data for a group of peer companies. We supplement this analysis with additional market information specific to each executive&#8217;s role and responsibilities, including information gleaned from our experience recruiting for executive positions at Microsoft. While this market analysis and supplemental data inform the decisions of the independent members of our Board and our Compensation Committee on the range of compensation opportunities, we do not tie Named Executive compensation to specific market percentiles. Further, because other companies actively recruit our executives to fill CEO and other senior leadership positions, we supplement market information with data on external opportunities potentially available to our executives. We also consider the relationship of annual target compensation among internal peers. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In setting our fiscal year 2026 compensation program design and compensation levels applicable to Named Executives, we considered pay practices at the largest technology companies. The Compensation Committee believes these companies&#8217; executives have comparably complex roles and responsibilities. Even so, our scale is multiple times larger than our median peer as shown in the charts below. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Peer Group Used for Fiscal Year 2026 Pay Analysis </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">For fiscal year 2026, the Compensation Committee reviewed the evolution of our business against our historical peer group, and as a result approved moving to the use of a single peer group of bellwether technology companies to reflect the increasing focus on high-technology talent and, in some cases, pay models, that more closely represent Microsoft&#8217;s more direct competitors for executive talent. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Fiscal Year 2026 Peer Group </span></span></p><div style="line-height:5.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div>

For fiscal year 2026: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

These targets are intended to be challenging but achievable. Our Compensation Committee then determines thresholds, maximums, and interim payout levels after considering historical data, upside/downside scenarios, sensitivity analysis, and year-over-year growth comparisons, to ensure rigorous alignment of payouts to performance. We set thresholds that we believe are reasonably achievable and maximums that we believe can be reached only with exceptional performance. Our Compensation Committee actively reviews the appropriateness of payout thresholds and maximums for each metric. Our Compensation Committee focuses on ensuring that our challenging goals, when achieved, will result in long-term shareholder value creation and, historically, our performance against these challenging goals has led to substantial returns to our shareholders. </p>

<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; border-top:6.00pt solid #0075c9">&#160;</p></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Focus on Pay for Performance </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Over 95% of the annual target compensation opportunity for our CEO is performance-based and over 50% for our other Named Executives. All Named Executive Officers had at least 80% of the annual target compensation delivered in the form of equity awards, with the average across all Named Executives over 85%, to incentivize a long-term focus and align their interests with those of our shareholders. </p>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;width:100%;border-spacing:0;margin:0 auto">


<tr>

<td style="width:33%"/>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom;width:1%"/>
<td style="width:33%"/>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom;width:1%"/>
<td style="width:32%"/></tr>


<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt">
<td style="vertical-align:bottom" colspan="5"> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-align:center">


<img src="g61756g41k41.jpg" alt="LOGO" style="width:6.93585in;height:2.52368in"/>
</p> <p style="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt;text-align:left">&#160;</p></td></tr>
</table> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_15"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Section&#160;4 &#8211; Fiscal Year 2026 Compensation Program Design </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Consistent with our philosophy, the compensation program for our Named Executives in fiscal year 2026 consisted of an annual base salary plus annual cash and equity incentives awarded under our Executive Incentive Plan (&#8220;Incentive Plan&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Annual cash incentives were performance-based, with 70% determined formulaically based on achievement against <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-established</span> financial targets for our CEO (50% for our other Named Executives) and 30% determined based on operational performance in three weighted performance categories for our CEO (50% for our other Named Executives). Our Compensation Committee and the independent members of our Board believe this allocation strengthens our CEO&#8217;s accountability to achieving results on the objective financial metrics that most closely align with our business strategy and provides a strong incentive for our other Named Executives to drive performance on those key initiatives, which we believe strongly contributes to our success. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Equity incentives under the Incentive Plan were allocated 100% to target PSAs for our CEO. Equity incentives under the Incentive Plan were allocated 50% to target PSAs and 50% to stock awards with four-year vesting (&#8220;SAs&#8221;) for our other Named Executives. Our Compensation Committee and the independent members of our Board believed the 100% PSA level for our CEO fully aligned his pay with Microsoft&#8217;s long-term performance, while the 50/50 balance between PSAs and SAs appropriately supported our long-term business goals and long-term retention incentives for our other Named Executives, while also aligning their interests with those of our shareholders. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Base Salaries </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Named Executives&#8217; base salaries are set to align with the scope and complexity of their roles, their capabilities, and competitive market conditions. </p>

All financial performance goals required meaningful year-over-year growth in order for the target awards to be achieved. The fiscal year 2026 Incentive Plan Revenue and Incentive Plan Operating Income performance targets were based on the Company&#8217;s fiscal year 2026 internal operating budget. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Operational Assessment </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The operational assessment portion of each Named Executive&#8217;s fiscal year 2026 annual cash incentives was determined based on evaluation of their individual contributions to the furtherance of financial, operational, strategic, and culture indicators in three performance categories. <div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_16"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Section&#160;5 &#8211; Fiscal Year 2026 Compensation Decisions and Results </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Named Executives were awarded the following compensation in fiscal year 2026: </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Fiscal Year 2026 Base Salaries </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As part of the annual review of target compensation opportunities, our Compensation Committee and, for Mr.&#160;Nadella, the independent members of our Board, reviewed the base salaries of our Named Executives in September 2025. The independent members of our Board did not increase the base salary of Mr.&#160;Nadella, which it continued to believe was reasonable and appropriate given his role, capabilities, and experience, as well as the Company&#8217;s relative scale and performance. Our Compensation Committee also did not increase the base salaries of any of the NEOs, except in the case of Mr.&#160;Numoto. We increased Mr.&#160;Numoto&#8217;s base salary from $800,000 to $850,000, based on a competitive market review. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Fiscal Year 2026 Cash Incentive Awards </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We did not increase our target cash incentive opportunities in fiscal year 2026 as a percentage of base salary, except in the case of Mr.&#160;Numoto. For fiscal year 2026, these opportunities were: Mr.&#160;Nadella &#8211; 300%; Ms.&#160;Hood &#8211; 250%; Mr.&#160;Althoff &#8211; 250%; Mr.&#160;Numoto&#160;&#8211; 225%; and Mr.&#160;Smith &#8211; 250%. We increased Mr.&#160;Numoto&#8217;s target cash incentive opportunity from 200% to 225% of base salary, based on a competitive market review. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Compensation Committee and, for Mr.&#160;Nadella, the independent members of our Board, determined the design and payouts of fiscal year 2026 cash incentive awards. These were based on two performance categories: financial results and operational performance results. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Financial Results </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The fiscal year 2026 financial performance measures are shown below, resulting in a weighted payout of 129.03% as a percentage of target. We note that our Incentive Plan Revenue result was 130.02% of target and Incentive Plan Operating Income result was 128.05% of target, which equated to a 16.00% and 18.27% fiscal year 2026 growth rate, respectively, further demonstrating our commitment to rigorous goal setting. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

Because the grant date of a PSA for financial reporting purposes occurs when the performance targets are set, and targets under our PSA awards are established annually, PSAs listed in the Summary Compensation Table and Grants of Plan-Based Awards table include portions of current and prior year PSA awards. In the Summary Compensation Table, the value of PSAs is calculated using a Monte-Carlo simulation valuation performed as of the date of grant for financial reporting purposes. For fiscal year 2026, the stock price appreciation and corresponding relative TSR outperformance resulted in a grant date fair value higher than target value. Changes in Microsoft&#8217;s stock price and other inputs in the Monte-Carlo simulation may cause awards to be above or below target in any given year. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Relative TSR Modifier </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The core metric results for the fiscal year 2024 PSAs were then subject to adjustment based on the relative TSR performance modifier, which compares our TSR for the three-fiscal year performance period to the TSR of the S&amp;P 500. Our absolute TSR for the performance period satisfied the PSA payout requirement that TSR be positive. Our TSR relative to the S&amp;P 500 was at the 46<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">th</sup>&#160;percentile of the S&amp;P&#160;500, which meets the at least 40<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">th</sup> percentile performance condition required to receive the 100.00% multiplier. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

The number of shares of common stock to be earned will be based on an assessment of (1)&#160;performance against the metric goals during the applicable performance period, and (2)&#160;Microsoft&#8217;s relative TSR during the period. Microsoft&#8217;s relative TSR will not increase the shares earned for a performance period unless Microsoft&#8217;s absolute TSR for the performance period is positive. The metrics and relative weights under the fiscal year 2025 and 2026 PSAs are set forth on page&#160;46 in the table labeled Fiscal Year 2024 PSA Core Metric Performance and Payout Percentages. </p> <p style="font-size:24pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_16a"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Section&#160;6 &#8211; Fiscal Year 2027 Executive Compensation Program Changes </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Changes to Fiscal Year 2027 Incentive Plan </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We are evolving our business strategy and are building the infrastructure and capabilities to lead in the AI era. Recognizing Microsoft&#8217;s leadership in the ongoing AI platform shift and the related challenges and opportunities, we have simplified our compensation program to ensure that our executives are motivated to drive Microsoft&#8217;s success in this key strategic priority. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">To emphasize the importance of this shift, we refined our fiscal year 2027 Incentive Plan to simplify the design while furthering alignment with market practice. In fiscal year 2027, the cash incentive metrics will be based solely on Company metrics, with an individual modifier. The individual modifier will be assessed holistically to reflect priorities based on role and will continue to include an assessment of the operational performance categories: security, product, customers&#160;&amp; stakeholders, and culture. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_17"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Section&#160;7 &#8211; Other Compensation Policies and Information </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">No Extraordinary Perquisites </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Named Executives are eligible for the same benefits available to our other full-time employees. In the U.S., our benefits include our section&#160;401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, health care plan, life insurance plans, and other welfare benefit programs. In addition to the standard benefits offered to all U.S. employees, we maintain a nonqualified deferred compensation plan for our U.S. executive officers and senior managers. This deferred compensation plan is unfunded, and participation is voluntary. The deferred compensation plan allows our Named Executives to defer their base salary, the cash portion of their Incentive Plan awards, and certain <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-hire</span> bonuses. We do not contribute to the deferred compensation plan. Named Executives are eligible for matching gifts for charitable donations above the maximum for our other full-time employees. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We believe that the personal safety and security of our senior executives is of the utmost importance to Microsoft and its shareholders. Pursuant to our executive security program and based on our assessment and monitoring of security risks, we may provide security services to certain senior executives. Security services include personal security services, which may include protection of family members, private aviation, and driver services. The independent members of the Board decided that it was in the best interests of the Company and its stakeholders to provide personal security services to Mr.&#160;Nadella and Mr.&#160;Smith due to security considerations arising from their respective roles. We view the security services provided to Mr.&#160;Nadella and Mr.&#160;Smith as an integral part of our risk management program. We view these as necessary and appropriate business expenses that arise from the nature of their employment responsibilities. Personal security services enable Mr.&#160;Nadella and Mr.&#160;Smith to focus on their duties to Microsoft while reducing security threats, and therefore, mitigate risks to our business. In accordance with applicable regulations, we have reported the aggregate incremental costs of such services in the &#8220;All Other Compensation&#8221; column of the Summary Compensation Table as required by Item 402 of Regulation <span style="white-space:nowrap">S-K.</span> We have also implemented an annual process to provide oversight of the nature and cost of executive security measures. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">During fiscal year 2026, we provided no other executive-only perquisites or other personal benefits to our Named Executives other than matching gifts made to charitable organizations. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Post-Employment Compensation </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Named Executives do not have employment contracts. No Named Executive is entitled to any payments or benefits following a change in control of Microsoft. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our Named Executives may be eligible for additional vesting of their outstanding SAs following termination of employment on the same terms as our other employees. Consistent with our policy for U.S. employees at all levels, our Named Executives who retire from Microsoft after age 65 or after age 55 with 15 years of continuous service and were hired prior to August&#160;1, 2023, are eligible for the continuation of vesting of outstanding SAs granted at the time of the annual rewards period if the award was granted over one year before the date of retirement. A <span style="white-space:nowrap">pro-rata</span> portion of PSA shares will also continue vesting if the retirement occurs more than one year after the beginning of the performance period. As of June&#160;30, 2026, of our Named Executives only Mr.&#160;Nadella, Mr.&#160;Numoto, and Mr.&#160;Smith were retirement eligible. All employees whose employment with Microsoft terminates due to death or total and permanent disability generally fully vest in their outstanding SAs. Our PSAs vest for the target number of shares upon death or total and permanent disability. The value of our Named Executives&#8217; SAs and PSAs that would have vested assuming a June&#160;30, 2026 termination of employment due to death or total and permanent disability, or due to retirement on that date, are set forth in the table at page&#160;57. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In addition, our Named Executives are eligible to participate in the Microsoft Senior Executive Severance Benefit Plan (&#8220;Severance Plan&#8221;). The Severance Plan was adopted to help ensure continuity and focus of key leaders by providing designated executives severance payments and benefits if their employment is terminated without cause. For purposes of the Severance Plan, &#8220;cause&#8221; means: (i)&#160;a conviction or plea of guilty or no contest to a felony or certain misdemeanors; (ii)&#160;engaging in gross misconduct; (iii)&#160;repeated failure to substantially perform the duties of the Named Executive&#8217;s role; (iv)&#160;violation of any securities laws; or (v)&#160;violation of Microsoft&#8217;s policies designed to prevent violations of law. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Severance Plan payments and benefits have four components &#8211; cash, stock vesting, continued health care, and outplacement assistance &#8211; all provided by Microsoft. Cash payments consist of: (i)&#160;a severance payment equal to 12 months&#8217; base salary plus target annual cash incentive award, payable in a lump sum within 60 days after termination of employment; and (ii)&#160;a <span style="white-space:nowrap">pro-rata</span> payment of the Named Executive&#8217;s target annual cash incentive award for the partial year of work, payable in a lump sum at the same time other Incentive Plan cash awards for the year are paid. Stock vesting applies to SAs and PSAs. SAs that otherwise would vest in the <span style="white-space:nowrap">12-month</span> period after employment terminates continue to vest. After the first year of the PSA performance period is completed, a <span style="white-space:nowrap">pro-rata</span> portion of any PSA shares will also vest, and the number of shares subject to <span style="white-space:nowrap">pro-ration</span> is the lesser of the target award shares or the shares that are otherwise earned and payable after the end of the performance period. Continued contributions to premiums for COBRA health care continuation coverage and outplacement assistance will be provided on the same terms as are available to other employees whose employment is terminated without cause. There is no <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">change-in-control</span></span> provision in the Severance Plan. To receive the Severance Plan payments and benefits, the Named Executive must execute a separation agreement that includes a release of claims in favor of Microsoft, confidentiality and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-disparagement</span> provisions, and <span style="white-space:nowrap">12-month</span> <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">non-compete/non-solicitation</span></span> restrictions. Our Named Executives&#8217; Severance Plan benefits assuming a termination of employment without cause on June&#160;30, 2026, are set forth in the table at page&#160;57. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Mr.&#160;Nadella participates in the Severance Plan on the same terms as our other executive officers. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Comprehensive Clawback Policy </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Accountability is a fundamental value of Microsoft. To reinforce this value through our executive compensation program, our executive officers, other senior officers, and our Chief Accounting Officer are subject to a comprehensive &#8216;no fault&#8217; executive compensation recovery (&#8220;clawback&#8221;) policy. Under this policy, our Compensation Committee may seek to recover payments of incentive compensation in the event of a restatement, as defined under the incentive-based compensation recovery provisions of the Dodd-Frank Act and the Nasdaq listing rules. Our Compensation Committee may also seek recovery of cash and equity incentive compensation whether time-based or performance-based, awarded during a period where a covered executive committed or was aware of or willfully blind to a significant legal or compliance violation, irrespective of whether such violation occurred in connection with a restatement. Our executive compensation recovery policy is available on our website at <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/policiesandguidelines</span>. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Robust Stock Ownership Policy </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Our executive officers and certain other senior executives are required to maintain a minimum equity stake in Microsoft. This policy embodies our Compensation Committee&#8217;s belief that our most senior executives should maintain a significant personal financial stake in Microsoft to promote a long-term perspective in managing our business. In addition, the policy helps align executive and shareholder interests, which reduces incentive for excessive short-term risk taking. Each covered executive is required to acquire and maintain ownership of shares of Microsoft common stock equal to a specified multiple of his or her base salary, which for our Named Executives ranges from 8 to 15 times base salary, as shown in the table below. Each covered executive must retain 50% of all net shares <span style="white-space:nowrap">(post-tax)</span> that vest until achieving his or her minimum share ownership requirement. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

Compensation to our Named Executives over this limit is nondeductible. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Annual&#160;Compensation&#160;Risk&#160;Assessment </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We performed an annual assessment for our Compensation and Audit and Finance Committees of our Board of Directors to determine whether the risks arising from our fiscal year 2026 compensation policies and practices were reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on Microsoft. Our assessment reviewed the material elements of executive and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</span> employee compensation. We concluded these policies and practices do not create risk that is reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on Microsoft. </p>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; border-top:6.00pt solid #0075c9">&#160;</p></td>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The structure of our compensation program for our executive officers does not incentivize unnecessary or excessive risk-taking. The base salary component of compensation does not encourage risk-taking because it is a fixed amount. The Incentive Plan awards have these risk-limiting characteristics:<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span> </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;width:100%;border-spacing:0;margin:0 auto">


<tr>

<td style="width:51%"/>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom;width:1%"/>
<td style="width:48%"/></tr>


<tr style="font-size:1pt">
<td style="height:3.75pt"/>
<td style="height:3.75pt" colspan="2"/></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt">
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Cash incentive awards under the Incentive Plan are limited to 200% of a&#160;target cash incentive award</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Cash incentive awards are structured 50% (70% for CEO) based on <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-established</span> goals (balance of growth and profitability goals) and 50% (30% for CEO) based on operational performance as assessed across three performance categories, diversifying the risk associated with any single aspect of performance</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">The majority of Incentive Plan award value is delivered in awards for shares of Microsoft common stock with multi-year vesting schedules or performance periods, which aligns the interests of our executive officers to long-term shareholder interests</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">We maintain robust executive stock ownership requirements ranging from 5x to 15x annual salary, which reduces incentive for excessive short-term risk taking</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">PSA metrics further diversify the elements of the program to minimize the incentive to produce any particular outcome</p></div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;&#160;</td>
<td style="padding-bottom:2pt ;vertical-align:bottom"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">PSAs use Company-wide measures that are not specific to any one executive officer&#8217;s sphere of responsibility and that apply equally to all participants to encourage a unified and responsible approach to achieving financial and strategic goals</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Overlapping performance periods for PSAs limit the impact of short-term business performance or share price fluctuations on final outcomes</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Equity awards are not made in the form of stock options, which may provide an asymmetrical incentive to take unnecessary or excessive risks to increase the market price of Microsoft common stock</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Members of our Compensation Committee (or for Mr.&#160;Nadella, the independent members of our Board of Directors) approve all Incentive Plan awards to executive officers, including performance achievement levels that determine final payout outcomes, and have the opportunity to reduce payments and use negative discretion, if appropriate</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt; display: table-row"><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial">&#8226;</p></div><div style="display: table-cell"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.594444em; font-family:Arial">Awards are subject to the Company&#8217;s Executive Compensation Recovery policy, which provides for recoupment in the event of a restatement or misconduct</p></div></div> <p style="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt">&#160;</p></td></tr>
</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Awards are subject to our Executive Compensation Recovery Policy, described in this Section&#160;7 &#8211; Other Compensation Policies and Information &#8211; Comprehensive Clawback Policy. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Executive officers are subject to our executive stock ownership requirements, described in this Section&#160;7 &#8211; Other Compensation Policies and Information &#8211; Robust Stock Ownership Policy. </p> <p style="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_18"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Compensation Committee Report </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Compensation Committee has reviewed and discussed with management the Compensation Discussion and Analysis provided above. Based on its review and discussions, the Compensation Committee recommended to the Board of Directors that the Compensation Discussion and Analysis be included in this Proxy Statement. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Compensation Committee </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Catherine MacGregor (Chair) </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Carmine Di Sibio </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Sandra E. <td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(1)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial;text-align:left">Includes the grant date fair values for SAs and PSAs calculated in accordance with Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) Topic 718 based on the market price of the shares subject to the award on the date of grant. The value of SAs is reduced by the present value of estimated future dividends because dividends are not paid on SA shares until vesting. The value of PSAs is calculated using a Monte-Carlo simulation valuation performed as of the date of grant by an independent third party. Because the grant date for a PSA occurs when performance targets are approved, and we approved performance targets in each of fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024, PSA values in this column include: (i)&#160;for fiscal year 2026 &#8211; 33.33% of each of the fiscal year 2026 PSAs, the fiscal year 2025 PSAs, and the fiscal year 2024 PSAs; (ii)&#160;for fiscal year 2025 &#8211; 33.33% of each of the fiscal year 2025 PSAs, the fiscal year 2024 PSAs, and the fiscal year 2023 PSAs; and (iii)&#160;for fiscal year 2024 &#8211; 33.33% of each of the fiscal year 2024 PSAs, the fiscal year 2023 PSAs, and the fiscal year 2022 PSAs. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

The threshold is calculated as if the threshold of only the least weighted metric (15% weight for fiscal year 2026) is met, and this amount is then reduced by 25% based on assumption that the maximum adjustment for Microsoft&#8217;s total shareholder return underperforming the S&amp;P 500 is applied. The value of SAs is reduced by the present value of estimated future dividends because dividends are not paid on SA shares until vesting. Values for PSAs in this column are calculated using a Monte Carlo simulation valuation performed as of the date of grant by an independent third party. Because the grant date for a PSA occurs when PSA performance targets are approved, the grant date fair value is calculated for the portion of the PSA for which performance targets were set in fiscal year 2026 (33.33% of each of the 2026, 2025, and 2024 PSAs). </p></td></tr></table>

Participation in the Deferred Compensation Plan is limited to U.S. senior managers, including our U.S. Named Executives. No withdrawals are permitted prior to the previously elected distribution date, other than withdrawals for certain severe financial hardships as permitted by applicable law. Amounts deferred under the Deferred Compensation Plan are credited with hypothetical investment earnings based on participant investment elections made from among deemed investment options available under the plan. </p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial;text-align:left">Termination without cause includes incremental value associated with retirement-based stock vesting of SAs: $1,695,749 for Mr.&#160;Numoto and $4,372,540 for Mr.&#160;Smith. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:24pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_26"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">CEO Pay Ratio </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">For fiscal year 2026, the annual total compensation for the median employee of the Company (other than our CEO) was $215,057 and the annual total compensation of our CEO was $90,628,977. Based on this information, for fiscal year 2026 the ratio of the annual total compensation of our CEO to the annual total compensation of the median employee was 421 to 1. We believe this ratio is a reasonable estimate calculated in a manner consistent with Item&#160;402(u) of Regulation <span style="white-space:nowrap">S-K</span> under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As permitted under the SEC disclosure rules, the same median-paid employee selected for the 2025 Proxy Statement has been identified as the median-paid employee for the second year in this 2026 Proxy Statement, as there were no significant changes in our employee population or to the median-paid employee&#8217;s compensation arrangements in fiscal year 2026 that would significantly impact the pay ratio disclosure. We identified our median employee from among our employees as of June&#160;30, 2025<span style="font-style:italic">.</span> To identify our median employee, we used a &#8220;total direct compensation&#8221; measure consisting of: (i)&#160;fiscal year 2025 annual base pay (salary or gross wages for hourly employees, excluding paid leave), which we annualized for any permanent employees who commenced work during the year, (ii)&#160;target bonuses and cash incentives payable for fiscal year 2025 (excluding allowances, relocation payments, and profit-sharing), and (iii)&#160;the dollar value of SAs and target PSAs granted in fiscal year 2025. Compensation amounts were determined from our human resources and payroll systems of record. Payments not made in U.S. dollars were converted to U.S. dollars using <span style="white-space:nowrap">12-month</span> average exchange rates for the year. To identify our median employee, we then calculated the total direct compensation for our global employee population and excluded employees at the median who had anomalous compensation characteristics. </p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 7pt; font-family: Arial; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">The dollar amounts reported represent the amount of &#8220;compensation actually paid,&#8221; as calculated in accordance with the Pay Versus Performance Rules. These dollar amounts do not reflect the actual amounts of compensation earned by or paid to our Named Executives during the applicable year. For purposes of calculating &#8220;compensation actually paid,&#8221; the fair value of equity awards is calculated in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718 using the same assumption methodologies used to calculate the grant date fair value of awards for purposes of the Summary Compensation Table (refer to &#8220;Named Executive Officer Compensation &#8211; Fiscal Year 2026 Compensation Tables &#8211; Summary Compensation Table&#8221; for additional information).<span style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><span style="font-style:italic;display:inline;"> </span></span>The &#8220;compensation actually paid&#8221; for fiscal years 2023 and 2022 has been updated from the amounts in Microsoft&#8217;s 2023 Proxy Statement to reflect the application of recent SEC guidance relating to retirement vesting treatment, which was issued following the filing of the 2023 Proxy Statement. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size: 4pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_28"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Equity Award Grant Practices </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:14pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft has not granted stock options or similar awards, other than options substituted in acquisitions, since 2003. During fiscal year 2026, no Named Executive was awarded stock options, no Named Executives held any Microsoft stock options, and Microsoft did not time the disclosure of material nonpublic information or grants for the purpose of affecting the value of executive compensation. </p> <p style="font-size:18pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_29"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Equity Compensation Plan Information </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">This table provides information about shares of Microsoft common stock that may be issued under our equity compensation plans approved by shareholders and plans not approved by shareholders (if any) as of June&#160;30, 2026. Under the 2026, 2017, and 2001 Stock Plans, no option or stock appreciation rights may be repriced, replaced, regranted through cancellation, repurchased for cash or other consideration, or modified without shareholder approval (except in connection with a change in our capitalization) if the effect would be to reduce the exercise price for the shares underlying the award. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

Our employees prepare these reports for our directors and executive officers using information obtained from them and from Microsoft&#8217;s records. Due to an administrative error, Amy L. Coleman, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer, was 16 days late in filing a Form 4 on October&#160;3, 2025, to report the grant of a stock award for 4,358 shares. Due to broker initiated-transactions that occurred without his direction, approval, or knowledge, Bradford L. Smith, Vice Chair and President, filed a Form 4 on December&#160;12, 2025, to report the acquisition of 3,842 shares of common stock on April&#160;23, 2025, and the subsequent disposition of those shares on April&#160;30, 2025 and May&#160;5, 2025; Mr.&#160;Smith has paid the Company the full amount of profit realized in connection with these short-swing transactions. </p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:25pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc61756_32">3. Audit and Finance Committee Matters &#8195; </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_33"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Audit and Finance Committee Report </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Charter and Responsibilities </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Audit and Finance Committee operates under a written charter adopted by the Board of Directors. It is available on our website at <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/policiesandguidelines</span>. The charter, which was last amended effective September&#160;16, 2026, includes a calendar that outlines the Committee&#8217;s duties and responsibilities. The Committee reviews the charter and calendar annually and works with the Board of Directors to amend them as appropriate to reflect the evolving needs of the Board and role of the Committee. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board has the ultimate authority for effective corporate governance, including oversight of the management of Microsoft. The Audit and Finance Committee assists the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities by overseeing the accounting and financial reporting processes of Microsoft, the audits of Microsoft&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and internal control over financial reporting, the qualifications and performance of the independent registered public accounting firm engaged as Microsoft&#8217;s independent auditor, and the performance of Microsoft&#8217;s internal auditor. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Audit and Finance Committee relies on the expertise and knowledge of management, the internal auditor, and the independent auditor in carrying out its oversight responsibilities. Management is responsible for the preparation, presentation, and integrity of Microsoft&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, accounting and financial reporting principles, internal control over financial reporting, and disclosure controls and procedures designed to ensure compliance with accounting standards, applicable laws, and regulations. Management is also responsible for objectively reviewing and evaluating the adequacy, effectiveness, and quality of Microsoft&#8217;s system of internal controls. Microsoft&#8217;s independent auditor, Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche LLP (&#8220;Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche&#8221;), is responsible for performing an independent audit of the consolidated financial statements and expressing an opinion on the conformity of those financial statements with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;). The independent auditor is also responsible for expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of Microsoft&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Fiscal Year 2026 Activity </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">For and during fiscal year 2026, the Audit and Finance Committee fulfilled its duties and responsibilities as outlined in the charter and the accompanying calendar. The Committee meets twice each quarter; once in connection with quarterly Board of Directors meetings and once to review the quarterly Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">10-Q</span> or annual Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">10-K.</span> In addition, the Committee meets as needed to address emerging accounting, compliance, or other matters, or for educational training. Specifically, the Committee: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Reviewed and discussed with management and the independent auditor Microsoft&#8217;s quarterly earnings press releases, consolidated financial statements, and related periodic reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Reviewed and discussed with management, the internal auditor, and the independent auditor, management&#8217;s assessment of the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting and the independent auditor&#8217;s opinion about the effectiveness of Microsoft&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Reviewed and discussed with management, the internal auditor, and the independent auditor, as appropriate, the audit scopes and plans of both the internal auditor and the independent auditor </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Inquired about significant business and financial reporting risks, reviewed Microsoft&#8217;s policies for risk assessment and risk management, and assessed the steps management is taking to control these risks </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Met in periodic executive sessions with each of management, the internal auditor, and the independent auditor to discuss the results of the examinations by the independent and internal auditors, their evaluations of internal controls, and the&#160;overall quality of the Company&#8217;s financial reporting, and any other matters as appropriate </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Reviewed with the Chief Compliance Officer legal and regulatory matters that may have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements or internal control over financial reporting </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Statements </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Audit and Finance Committee has reviewed and discussed with management and the independent auditor Microsoft&#8217;s audited consolidated financial statements and related footnotes for the fiscal year ended June&#160;30, 2026, and the independent auditor&#8217;s&#160;report on those financial statements. Management represented to the Committee that Microsoft&#8217;s consolidated financial statements were prepared in accordance with GAAP. Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche presented the matters required to be discussed with the Committee by Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (&#8220;PCAOB&#8221;) standards and Rule <span style="white-space:nowrap">2-07</span> of SEC <span style="white-space:nowrap">Regulation&#160;S-X.</span> This review included a discussion with management and the independent auditor of the quality (not&#160;merely the&#160;acceptability) of Microsoft&#8217;s accounting principles, the reasonableness of significant estimates and judgments, and the disclosures in Microsoft&#8217;s consolidated financial statements, including the disclosures relating to critical accounting policies. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Based on the reviews and discussions described above, the Audit and Finance Committee recommended to the Board of Directors that the audited consolidated financial statements be included in Microsoft&#8217;s Annual Report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">10-K</span> for the fiscal year ended June&#160;30, 2026, for filing with the SEC. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Independent Auditor Tenure and Rotation </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As part of its auditor engagement process, the Audit and Finance Committee considers whether to rotate the independent audit firm. Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche has been Microsoft&#8217;s independent auditor since the Company&#8217;s initial public offering in 1986. The Audit and Finance Committee believes that our long-term engagement of Deloitte has several benefits, including enhanced audit quality due to Deloitte&#8217;s significant institutional knowledge of our business, accounting policies and practices, and internal control over financial reporting, and elimination of time and expense inherent in onboarding a new independent auditor. Deloitte rotates its lead audit engagement partner every five years; the Audit and Finance Committee interviews proposed candidates and selects the lead audit engagement partner. Pursuant to this process, the Committee selected a new Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche lead audit engagement partner beginning with the fiscal year 2025 audit.&#160;The Audit and Finance Committee believes there are significant benefits to having an independent auditor with an extensive history with the Company. These include: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Higher quality audit work and accounting advice due to Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche&#8217;s institutional knowledge of our business and operations, accounting policies and financial systems, and internal control framework </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Operational efficiencies and a resulting lower fee structure because of Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche&#8217;s history and familiarity with our business </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Independence and Performance of Outside Audit Firm </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Audit and Finance Committee recognizes the importance of maintaining the independence of Microsoft&#8217;s independent auditor, both in fact and appearance, and takes a number of measures to ensure independence. The Committee leads the selection of the lead audit engagement partner, working with Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche with input from management. The Committee has established a policy pursuant to which all services, audit and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-audit,</span> provided by the independent auditor must be <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-approved</span> by the Committee or its delegate. This policy prohibits the independent auditor from providing <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</span> services such as bookkeeping or financial systems design and implementation. The Company&#8217;s <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-approval</span> policy is more fully described below in this Part 3 &#8211; Policy on Audit and Finance Committee <span style="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Approval</span> of Audit and Permissible <span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-Audit</span> Services of Independent Auditor. The Committee has concluded that the amount and nature of those services provided was compatible with maintaining the independence of Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche. In addition, Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche has provided the Committee with the written disclosures and letter required by applicable requirements of the PCAOB regarding the independent accountant&#8217;s communications with the Audit and Finance Committee concerning independence. The Committee has reviewed these materials and discussed the firm&#8217;s independence with Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche. </p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Audit-Related Fees </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Audit-related fees consist of assurance and related services that are reasonably related to the performance of the audit or review of Microsoft&#8217;s consolidated financial statements or internal control over financial reporting. This category may include fees related to the performance of audits and attest services not required by statute or regulations; audits of our employee benefit plans; due diligence related to mergers, acquisitions, and investments; additional revenue and license compliance procedures related to the performance of review or audit of Microsoft&#8217;s consolidated financial statements; third-party assurance audits for cloud services; and accounting consultations about the application of GAAP to proposed transactions. Revenue assurance and license compliance includes procedures under contracts we have entered that provide for review by an independent accountant, and advice about controls associated with the completeness and accuracy of our software licensing revenue. These services support the evaluation of the effectiveness of internal control over revenue recognition and enhance the independent auditor&#8217;s understanding of our licensing programs and controls. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Tax Fees </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Tax fees generally consist of tax compliance and return preparation, and tax planning and advice. Tax compliance and return preparation services consist of preparing original and amended tax returns and claims for refunds. Tax planning and advice services consist of support during income tax audits or inquiries. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">All Other Fees </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">All other fees consist of permitted services other than those that meet the criteria above and include training activities, and subscriptions and surveys on economic, industry, accounting, and human resources topics. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Audit and Finance Committee concluded that the provision of the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</span> services listed above is compatible with maintaining the independence of Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche. </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_35"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Policy on Audit and Finance Committee <span style="white-space:nowrap">Pre-Approval</span> of Audit and Permissible <span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-Audit</span> Services of Independent Auditor </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Audit and Finance Committee has a policy for <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-approval</span> of all audit and permissible <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-audit</span> services provided by the independent auditor. Each year, the Committee approves the terms on which the independent auditor is engaged for the ensuing fiscal year. At least quarterly, the Committee reviews and, if appropriate, <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-approves</span> services to be performed by the independent auditor, reviews a report summarizing fiscal <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">year-to-date</span></span> services provided by the independent auditor, and reviews an updated projection of the fiscal year&#8217;s estimated fees. The Committee, as permitted by its <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-approval</span> policy, from time to time delegates the approval of certain permitted services or classes of services to a member of the Committee. The Committee then reviews the delegate&#8217;s approval decisions each quarter. Microsoft uses a centralized internal system to collect requests from Company personnel for services by the independent auditor to facilitate compliance with this <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-approval</span> policy. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>
