 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc61756_38">Proposal&#160;2:&#160;Advisory&#160;Vote&#160;to&#160;Approve Named Executive Officer Compensation </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Pursuant to Section&#160;14A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, we are asking for your advisory vote on the following resolution <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">(&#8220;say-on-pay</span></span> vote&#8221; resolution): </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">&#8220;Resolved, that the shareholders approve, in a nonbinding vote, the compensation paid to the Company&#8217;s Named Executive Officers, as disclosed in Part 2 &#8211; Named Executive Officer Compensation.&#8221; </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Receipt of a majority of the votes cast is required to approve this proposal. We hold our <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">say-on-pay</span></span> vote every year and expect to hold another <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">say-on-pay</span></span> vote at our 2027 Annual Meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As described in detail in Part&#160;2 &#8211; Named Executive Officer Compensation, we design our executive compensation program to attract, motivate, and retain the key executives who drive our success and industry leadership while considering Company and individual performance and alignment with the long-term interests of our shareholders. Please read the &#8220;Compensation Discussion and Analysis&#8221; and the compensation tables and narrative disclosure that follow it for additional details about our executive compensation program. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Our Board of Directors recommends a vote FOR approval, on a <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-binding,</span> advisory basis, of the compensation paid to our Named Executive Officers. </span></span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc61756_39">Proposal&#160;3:&#160;Ratification&#160;of&#160;the&#160;Selection&#160;of&#160;Deloitte&#160;&amp;&#160;Touche&#160;LLP as our Independent Auditor for Fiscal Year 2027 </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Audit and Finance Committee has selected Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche LLP as Microsoft&#8217;s independent auditor for fiscal year 2027. The Board asks shareholders to ratify that selection. Although current law, rules, and regulations, and the charter of the Audit and Finance Committee require the Audit and Finance Committee to engage, retain, and supervise Microsoft&#8217;s independent auditor, the Board considers the selection of the independent auditor to be an important matter of shareholder concern and is submitting the selection of Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche for ratification by shareholders as a matter of good corporate practice. As described in Part 3 &#8211; Audit and Finance Committee Matters, the Board considers the selection of Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche as Microsoft&#8217;s independent auditor for fiscal year 2027 to be in the best interests of Microsoft and its shareholders. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Receipt of a majority of the votes cast is required to approve this proposal. If the selection of Deloitte&#160;&amp; Touche is not ratified, the Audit and Finance Committee will consider the result a recommendation to consider selection of a different firm. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">The Board of Directors recommends a vote FOR the ratification of the independent auditor. </span></span></span></p>

<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <div style="line-height:1.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #0075c9">&#160;</div> <p style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14pt; font-family:Arial" id="toc61756_41"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Shareholder Proposals </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Receipt of a majority of the votes cast is required to approve each of the following shareholder proposals. We will furnish the address and number of shares held by the proponents of any of the following shareholder proposals upon receipt of a request to the Corporate Secretary for such information. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Because the Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;) no longer provides substantive views on most shareholder proposal exclusion requests, responsibility for exclusion determinations now rests primarily with companies. Microsoft has established a documented review process involving management, the Governance and Nominating Committee, and outside counsel to evaluate potential exclusions. The process considers a number of factors, including applicable law, shareholder interests, governance implications, and the Company&#8217;s commitment to transparency. Where appropriate, the Company may include proposals in its proxy materials notwithstanding the availability of potential exclusion arguments. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Information about submitting shareholder proposals for the 2027 Annual Shareholder Meeting is provided on page 84. For shareholder proposals for the 2027 Annual Shareholders Meeting, Microsoft will apply submission and resubmission thresholds in effect under <span style="white-space:nowrap">SEC&#160;Rule&#160;14a-8</span> as in effect on January&#160;1, 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold" id="toc61756_40">Proposal&#160;4:&#160;Additional Disclosures Meeting Climate Commitments </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Trillium Asset Management and a <span style="white-space:nowrap">co-filer</span> have advised us that they intend to submit the following proposal for consideration at the Annual Meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Whereas: Climate change-driven impacts could erase trillions in global GDP by 2050.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">1</sup><sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">,</sup><sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) is compounding these risks, as generative AI is driving energy demand and increasing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with data centers, which are projected to consume 9 &#8211;17&#160;percent of U.S. electricity generation by 2030.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> Embodied carbon in building materials is also a significant source of emissions linked to data centers.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">4</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft has built a reputation for climate leadership by setting 2030 targets to halve its GHG emissions and achieve hourly matching of its electricity consumption with clean energy. However, the company&#8217;s emissions have increased by 23&#160;percent over its 2020 baseline,<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">5</sup> are predicted to climb significantly,<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">6</sup> and it has yet to disclose hourly matching data. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">It is precisely because of the company&#8217;s established leadership that investors seek to understand how Microsoft will sustain its credibility, given that failing to meet its targets could expose it to operational and reputational risks. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Poor climate performance may put Microsoft&#8217;s brand value at risk. According to the consultancy Brand Finance and the 2025 Sustainability Perceptions Index, the total amount of brand value tied to consumer belief in Microsoft&#8217;s sustainability was valued at $22.7&#160;billion in 2024, second only to Apple.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">7</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Additionally, Microsoft identifies attracting and retaining talent as a key driver of success.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">8</sup> A 2025 Deloitte survey found that 70&#160;percent of Gen Z and Millennial workers consider a company&#8217;s environmental credentials when evaluating employers.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">9</sup> Because these cohorts likely dominate Microsoft&#8217;s talent pipeline, underperformance on environmental commitments could limit access to critical talent. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft is also issuing a record-breaking amount of debt to fund data center expansion.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">10</sup> Some studies indicate that companies with favorable reputations and higher management credibility may experience better access to and lower costs of capital, meaning that Microsoft&#8217;s ability to credibly execute on its climate commitments may prove material in the future.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">11</sup><sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">,</sup><sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">12</sup> Enhanced disclosure would allow investors to evaluate whether the company is maintaining its credibility and efficient access to capital. </p><div style="line-height:8.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;width:11%">&#160;</div>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:7pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Given this, Microsoft could better inform investors by providing: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Contingency plans and stress tests of Microsoft&#8217;s strategies for achieving its climate commitments, assessing factors over which it has direct and indirect control<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">1</sup> </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Scenario analyses that evaluate factors that could negatively impact the company&#8217;s emissions reduction progress<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">The company&#8217;s anticipated near-term emissions pathway<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Efforts to reduce enabled emissions associated with use of Microsoft&#8217;s AI products developed for extraction of fossil fuels </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left">Hourly clean energy matching data </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Resolved: </span>Given the company&#8217;s growing GHG emissions and the challenge of meeting its goals, shareholders request Microsoft disclose <span style="font-style:italic">additional information</span> illustrating how it will manage its climate commitments. This disclosure should be beyond existing disclosures, at reasonable cost, omitting proprietary information, and made annually. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Board Recommendation </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">The Board of Directors recommends a vote AGAINST the proposal for the following reasons: </span></span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">COMPANY STATEMENT IN OPPOSITION </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft is committed to transparency regarding our corporate-level environmental commitments and our progress toward achieving them. We believe our current disclosures already provide shareholders with extensive decision-useful information regarding Microsoft&#8217;s climate strategy, governance, potential risks, opportunities, performance against goals, and progress toward our environmental targets. The proposal does not identify an information gap that could prevent investors from evaluating Microsoft&#8217;s climate-related performance or oversight. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft established its ambitious climate and sustainability goals in 2020, and since then has provided extensive public reporting regarding the actions we are taking to achieve them. We disclose our greenhouse gas emissions, energy use, renewable energy procurement efforts, carbon removal portfolio, governance processes, key climate risks, and our progress toward our environmental commitments in numerous voluntary and regulatory disclosures which are publicly available and posted at <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/transparency</span>. This includes our annual Environmental Sustainability Report, sustainability websites, reporting to CDP (formerly the Carbon Disclosure Project), climate-reporting aligned to standards from the International Sustainability Standards Board, regulatory disclosures such as California&#8217;s Voluntary Carbon Market Disclosures Act, and other public disclosures, including reporting on progress towards our approved near-term Science Based Target. Microsoft will also begin reporting under additional climate disclosure requirements from Australia, California, the European Union, and other jurisdictions as soon as October 2026, which will further supplement our environmental disclosures. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Importantly, in our 2026 Environmental Sustainability Report and other disclosures, Microsoft has been transparent not only about areas of progress but also about areas where achieving our goals has become more complex. We have publicly reported increases in emissions associated with the growth of our business, including the expansion of AI and cloud infrastructure, and continue to explain the investments and innovations we are pursuing to address those challenges. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft&#8217;s climate strategy is overseen through established governance and risk-management processes that evaluate environmental, operational, financial, legal, and reputational considerations across the business. Consistent with those processes, we regularly assess climate-related risks and opportunities and disclose material information to investors through our existing reporting. Requiring a separate, stand-alone report focused on speculative future outcomes would not meaningfully enhance shareholder understanding beyond the extensive information already available. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The proposal does not demonstrate that Microsoft&#8217;s existing disclosures are insufficient for investors to evaluate the company&#8217;s climate-related strategy, governance, potential risks, opportunities, and performance. Instead, it requests a collection of new disclosures that extend beyond not just legal and regulatory requirements, but beyond established voluntary climate-reporting frameworks and the types of disclosures commonly observed among peer companies. Among other things, the proposal seeks hypothetical scenario analyses, contingency plans, stress testing, anticipated emissions pathways, and other forward-looking information that is inherently uncertain and subject to change as technologies, market conditions, energy systems, and regulatory environments evolve. We remain focused on our Sustainability Report and other environmental reporting while also meeting new disclosure mandates arising globally. </p><div style="line-height:8.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;width:11%">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.86em; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial">AUDIT&#160;AND<br/>FINANCE&#160;COMMITTEE MATTERS</p></td>

<td style="vertical-align:top"><span style="font-size:21pt;color:#0075c9">4</span></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.86em; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9">PROPOSALS&#160;TO<br/>BE&#160;VOTED&#160;ON&#160;DURING<br/>THE MEETING</span></p></td>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.86em; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial">INFORMATION&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;<br/>ABOUT THE<br/>MEETING</p></td></tr>

<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; border-top:6.00pt solid #0075c9">&#160;</p></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Proposal&#160;5:&#160;Report on Human Rights Due Diligence </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Religious of the Sacred Heart of Mary and <span style="white-space:nowrap">co-filers</span> have advised us that they intend to submit the following proposal for consideration at the Annual Meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">RESOLVED</span>:<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>Shareholders request the Board of Directors publish a report, at reasonable cost and omitting proprietary information, assessing the effectiveness of Microsoft&#8217;s human rights due diligence (&#8220;HRDD&#8221;) processes in preventing, identifying, and addressing customer misuse of Microsoft artificial intelligence (&#8220;AI&#8221;) and cloud products or services that violates human rights or international humanitarian law (&#8220;IHL&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (&#8220;UNGPs&#8221;) constitute the global authoritative framework outlining human rights responsibilities of businesses, and expectations are heightened for companies with business activities in conflict-affected and high-risk areas.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">1</sup> Companies are expected to take all reasonable steps to ensure their products and services are not used to violate human rights<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> and to transparently report on the effectiveness of their HRDD.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft states it conducts ongoing HRDD across its value chain, in line with its obligations under the UNGPs, but recent allegations and findings of severe customer misuse suggest Microsoft&#8217;s HRDD is ineffective.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">4</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">For example, several reports have detailed Israel&#8217;s alleged use of Microsoft&#8217;s AI and cloud services and technologies in its attacks against Palestinians,<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">5</sup> which have been labeled war crimes and crimes against humanity.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">6</sup> Many prominent international organizations and scholars believe these attacks constitute genocide.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">7</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In June 2026, Microsoft confirmed claims by The Guardian that Microsoft&#8217;s cloud was being used to store mass surveillance data on Palestinians, which led Microsoft to terminate one specific contract with an Israeli military unit.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">8</sup> Importantly, it was The Guardian, not Microsoft&#8217;s own HRDD, that identified the misuse, which was based on &#8220;information [Microsoft] could not access.&#8221;<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">9</sup> Concerningly, Microsoft&#8217;s initial May 2025 internal assessments and external review found no evidence of misuse, while acknowledging it lacked &#8220;visibility into how customers use our software on their own servers or other devices.&#8221;<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">10</sup> This example highlights ineffective HRDD and suggests Microsoft may be unable to identify other instances of serious human rights or IHL violations. Microsoft still maintains extensive contracts with the Israeli military, purportedly connected to ongoing human rights violations against Palestinians.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">11</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Additionally, reports raise concerns about Microsoft&#8217;s cloud being used by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (&#8220;ICE&#8221;) in &#8220;facilitating an immigration crackdown.&#8221;<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">12</sup> Although Microsoft says it &#8220;do[es] not believe&#8221; its cloud is being used by ICE for mass surveillance, Microsoft employees have filed internal ethics reports highlighting these concerns.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">13</sup> Microsoft also has a close partnership with Palantir Technologies, Inc.,<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">14</sup> which uses Microsoft&#8217;s cloud for its software and which has been linked to severe constitutional and human rights violations in the context of immigration enforcement.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">15</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Ineffective HRDD exposes Microsoft to material legal, operational, and reputational risks, some of which have already materialized: outspoken opposition from its own employees,<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">16</sup> a boycott and divestment campaign,<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">17</sup> an EU General Data Protection Regulation (&#8220;GDPR&#8221;) related to Palestinian human rights violations,<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">18</sup> and severe reputational damage. </p><div style="line-height:8.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;width:11%">&#160;</div>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Board Recommendation </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">The Board of Directors recommends a vote AGAINST the proposal for the following reasons: </span></span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">COMPANY STATEMENT IN OPPOSITION </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft has a long-standing commitment to human rights outlined in its Global Human Rights Statement. As part of this commitment, we conduct ongoing human rights due diligence consistent with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (&#8220;UNGPs&#8221;), the Organisation for Economic <span style="white-space:nowrap">Co-operation</span> and Development (&#8220;OECD&#8221;) Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises, and other international standards. These processes are continuous and integrated into our operations to support us in identifying, understanding, and addressing human rights risks across our business. This work is informed by regular engagement with independent human rights experts and lessons learned over time, which helps us to continually adapt and strengthen our processes as technology and our business evolve. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Given this comprehensive approach, the Board believes the additional report requested by the shareholder proposal is unnecessary. Microsoft already does what the proposal seeks: it conducts rigorous, ongoing human rights due diligence and reports publicly on how the program works and how we act on what we learn. We assess effectiveness on an ongoing basis through internal evaluation and ongoing engagement with independent human rights experts and external stakeholders, including from civil society, academia, the investor community, industry, governments, and international organizations. Through this engagement, we aim to learn and share information about critical issues at the intersection of technology and human rights, which we believe is important to advancing our own efforts and those of the wider technology ecosystem. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft produces a robust annual human rights report detailing our policies and their application, including evolution over time, and numerous additional reports such as those providing detailed <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">country-by-country</span></span> data on our responses to law enforcement requests for customer information and government and other requests for content removal. In June 2026, Microsoft published a report summarizing an external investigation by Covington&#160;&amp; Burling LLP and the <span style="white-space:nowrap">follow-up</span> actions we are taking to strengthen our governance and oversight. (See <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/2025InvestigationSummary</span>) </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Finally, we have published stand-alone disclosures on specific topics, including executive summaries of human rights impact assessments (&#8220;HRIAs&#8221;). We continue to work to enhance these disclosures over time, but believe the specific stand-alone report requested in this proposal is unnecessary and duplicative of existing reporting. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Our commitment to ongoing human rights due diligence </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft is committed to conducting continuous human rights due diligence worldwide, in line with the UNGPs. This commitment is explained in our Global Human Rights Statement (see <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/humanrights</span>). Key features of our program include: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">Regular Risk Assessments: </span>We conduct ongoing human rights due diligence, including HRIAs at multiple levels (enterprise-wide, for specific products, deals, or relationships, and in sensitive regions) to identify actual or potential salient human rights risks and impacts that we may cause or contribute to or be directly linked to, either through our own activities or as a result of our business relationships. For complex business questions, HRIAs are often conducted by independent experts in business and human rights. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In calendar years 2024 and 2025, we commissioned an independent corporate human rights saliency assessment to evaluate our <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">end-to-end</span></span> operations and affirm our priority areas of focus. The findings guide our risk management, mitigation, and remediation efforts and inform our internal training, governance structures, and operational safeguards. In tandem, we commissioned an independent HRIA of generative AI. These assessments involved stakeholder input and guide our risk mitigation strategies. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We apply our human rights due diligence approach to business decision-making across issues including data center siting, <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-sales</span> contract reviews, new product or feature developments, and sensitive AI deployments. These reviews are designed to mitigate risks before a deployment proceeds, not only to detect them afterward. However, we recognize that not all risks are foreseeable, and technology is deployed and used in dynamic contexts. We value the role that external stakeholders, including civil society and others, play in alerting us to issues, and we place emphasis on ongoing engagement and mechanisms and reporting channels that inform our due diligence efforts and actions. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">Integration into Business Processes:</span> Human rights considerations are embedded into Microsoft&#8217;s policies and daily operations. Contractual terms prohibit misuse of our services to violate rights. Cross-functional teams work together to incorporate human rights safeguards in product design, market entry decisions, and supply chain management. This enables us to integrate rights-related considerations in core decision-making. </p></td></tr></table>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">External Perspectives: </span>Microsoft conducts regular engagement and consultation with external stakeholders including vulnerable populations or their trusted representatives to understand their perspectives and experiences. We also consult frequently with human rights experts to identify human rights risks and mitigation measures. Engagement is conducted through formal meetings, participation in multistakeholder fora, focus groups, surveys, and direct interviews. It is a key component of our human rights due diligence and risk management process, and the company&#8217;s human rights team includes a role primarily focused on stakeholder engagement. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">Continuous Improvement: </span>Our due diligence is <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-going</span> and adaptive. We update assessments when conditions change and learn from new challenges to refine our approach. Findings are assigned to accountable teams, tracked to implementation, and reported to governance bodies, so that mitigations are incorporated and learnings translate into concrete advancements in our policies, products, and customer relationships. This continuous cycle of <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">assess-act-review</span></span> epitomizes the UNGP concept of due diligence as a dynamic process, not a <span style="white-space:nowrap">one-off</span> report. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Transparency and ongoing expert engagement </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft provides extensive transparency about our human rights practices, and our program is continually informed by independent human rights experts. These disclosures demonstrate accountability for the effectiveness of our human rights due diligence. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">Extensive Public Reporting: </span>Microsoft has a strong track record of publicly reporting on its human rights commitments, processes, and progress. In December 2025, the company published its Human Rights Transparency Report, for the first time bringing together our legacy supply chain and human rights reports for a full value-chain review of human rights. This annual report details how we manage our salient human rights issues and what actions we took over the year. The report covering fiscal year 2026 will be published in December 2026. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">Other public channels: </span>Beyond the standalone human rights report, Microsoft communicates human rights due diligence through other channels, including our Global Human Rights Statement, a dedicated human rights website, and summaries of HRIAs and other due diligence. We regularly publish transparency reports at <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/transparency</span>, including our Responsible AI Transparency Report, Environmental Sustainability Report, and additional transparency reports. Updates are also published regularly through our blogs and other public communication channels, covering topics like data center siting in rights-challenged markets and our approach to responsible AI, demonstrating how human rights due diligence is applied in specific contexts.<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span> </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Engagement with independent experts and assessments </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We regularly consult independent human rights experts and participate in multistakeholder initiatives, which bring outside perspective to our due diligence and help us identify where to improve. Our corporate saliency assessment, repeated at regular intervals and conducted by independent business and human rights experts, provides a complete enterprise review of our practices. We participate in regulatory reporting that requires disclosure of our risk management and due diligence frameworks. Microsoft also undertakes voluntary assessments, such as our regular Global Network Initiative (&#8220;GNI&#8221;) Assessment, which involves a review by an accredited independent assessor to evaluate whether Microsoft is making a good faith effort to implement the GNI Principles on freedom of expression and privacy, with improvement over time. GNI publishes public assessment reports on its website. Beyond our regular assessments, Microsoft has also publicly shared a report summarizing an external investigation by Covington&#160;&amp; Burling LLP and the <span style="white-space:nowrap">follow-up</span> actions we are taking to strengthen our governance and oversight. (See <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/2025InvestigationSummary</span>) </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Conclusion </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Effective due diligence is not a <span style="white-space:nowrap">one-time</span> certification: it is a continuous process of identifying and assessing new information, investigating credible concerns, and taking action when warranted. Microsoft, like other technology providers, does not have visibility into every activity that customers conduct on their own systems. Our due diligence therefore relies on multiple, reinforcing mechanisms, including contractual terms prohibiting misuse of our services, risk assessments to identify, assess, and mitigate issues, <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-contract</span> gating for sensitive features, escalation and investigation processes, ongoing engagement with independent experts and affected stakeholders, and prompt review of credible new information. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">When concerns have been raised about how our technology is used, including in high-risk and conflict settings, we have investigated, engaged outside experts, published our findings, and, where warranted, changed or suspended our provision of services to customers. We have also fed learnings into ongoing process, policy, and procedure within our company. Most recently, we published a summary of the findings from that review (see <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/mideastreviewupdate</span>). The same escalation, review, and remediation process applies across our customer relationships, regardless of sector or geography. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Under the UNGPs, credible information from external sources is a designed input to due diligence, not a substitute for it: a process that surfaces a concern, investigates it, and acts on it is a process that is working. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Because Microsoft already reports on how its due diligence works, engages independent third-party experts, assessors, and external stakeholders, and provides transparency on how it responds when concerns arise, the requested report would be duplicative. We will continue to refine and communicate our human rights efforts as part of our ongoing governance and transparency reporting. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Proposal&#160;6:&#160;Report on Data Operations in Human Rights and Conflict Hotspots </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Azzad Asset Management, Inc. has advised us that they intend to submit the following proposal for consideration at the Annual Meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Resolved: Shareholders request the Board of Directors commission a report assessing the implications of siting Microsoft cloud data centers in countries of significant human rights concern, and the Company&#8217;s strategies for mitigating these impacts. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The report, prepared at reasonable cost and omitting confidential and proprietary information, should be published on the Company&#8217;s website within a year of the 2026 shareholders meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Supporting Statement: </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Shareholders are concerned by Microsoft&#8217;s plans to maintain and expand data center operations in locations that present significant human rights challenges. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Of particular note is the building of new data center capacity in Saudi Arabia and UAE, as well as the company&#8217;s existing data operations in Israel, and the issues around data security and surveillance that they give rise to. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">All three governments have been linked to significant human rights concerns relating to surveillance, privacy, and freedom of expression. Freedom House has documented extensive surveillance authorities, restrictions on online expression, and government access to communications data in Saudi Arabia and the UAE.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">1</sup> Microsoft&#8217;s provision of cloud and AI services to the Israeli government and military has likewise generated significant scrutiny, including allegations concerning surveillance of Palestinians, the storage and processing of surveillance-related data, and a GDPR complaint filed with Irish data protection authorities in 2025.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">These concerns also present material risks to shareholders. Microsoft has announced plans to invest at least $80&#160;billion in <span style="white-space:nowrap">AI-enabled</span> infrastructure, more than half in the United States, based on assumptions regarding future compute demand, energy consumption, and AI architectures that remain uncertain. Long-lived investments in jurisdictions presenting significant human rights, governance, and geopolitical risks may expose the Company to stranded assets, litigation, sanctions, regulatory action, operational disruptions, and reputational harm. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Although Microsoft states that it conducts human rights due diligence, stakeholder engagement, and HRIAs where appropriate, investors remain unable to assess the effectiveness of these processes because the company provides little information regarding where such assessments have been conducted, which stakeholders were consulted, what risks were identified, or how those risks were mitigated.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> Its recent review of the Israeli Ministry of Defense relationship addressed specific <span style="white-space:nowrap">customer-use</span> allegations, not the broader human rights implications of operating cloud infrastructure in countries of significant human rights concern.<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">4</sup> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">A report sufficient to fulfill the proposal&#8217;s essential objectives would examine the scope, implementation, and robustness of the company&#8217;s human rights due diligence processes for siting cloud computing operations. It would assess, consistent with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, and the Global Network Initiative Principles, how the company identifies, prevents, mitigates, and tracks impacts related to privacy, freedom of expression, and government access to data in conflict-affected or high-risk environments. </p><div style="line-height:8.0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:2pt;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;width:11%">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.86em; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9">PROPOSALS&#160;TO<br/>BE&#160;VOTED&#160;ON&#160;DURING<br/>THE MEETING</span></p></td>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.86em; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial">INFORMATION&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;<br/>ABOUT THE<br/>MEETING</p></td></tr>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; border-top:6.00pt solid #0075c9">&#160;</p></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Board Recommendation </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">The Board of Directors recommends a vote AGAINST the proposal for the following reasons: </span></span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">COMPANY STATEMENT IN OPPOSITION </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The requested report is not necessary because Microsoft&#8217;s existing disclosures sufficiently address how the company manages the key human rights risks raised by the proposal. While the proposal seeks additional operational detail that it says it does not find in existing disclosures, Microsoft management and the Board believe shareholders have sufficient information to understand the Company&#8217;s approach and oversight of its human rights risks without requiring disclosure of sensitive site-specific assessments or security-related information. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft provides meaningful information regarding its human rights commitments and efforts, including its governance and oversight, programmatic approach, efforts to conduct stakeholder engagement, ongoing due diligence, and mitigation processes. Microsoft shares information publicly about these efforts in its annual Human Rights Transparency Report, on its website, and through summaries of its corporate human rights assessments which are updated periodically. Microsoft also participates in a variety of required and voluntary rights-related assessment and reporting processes. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Demand for cloud and AI services continues to grow globally as governments, enterprises, and communities increasingly rely on digital technologies to drive economic development and innovation. Customers, particularly multinational organizations, often seek local cloud infrastructure to meet performance, regulatory, and data sovereignty requirements. Microsoft and other cloud providers operate datacenters in numerous countries around the world to support local economies, expand access to digital technologies, and comply with laws governing where data may be stored and processed. Consistent with Microsoft&#8217;s mission, we work to bring the benefits of AI and cloud computing to customers globally while maintaining robust processes to identify and address human rights, security, privacy, and other risks. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As we detail below, Microsoft&#8217;s infrastructure investment decisions are subject to extensive review involving business, operational, legal, regulatory, security, and risk-management considerations. Human rights considerations are one important input among many factors evaluated. The proposal incorrectly suggests that infrastructure investment decisions are made without consideration of long-term geopolitical and operational risks. Reviews weigh the long-term geopolitical, regulatory, and operational risks the proposal raises, including the possibility that conditions in a market change after an investment is made. Where they do, we may adjust the services we offer, the customers we serve, and where customer data is stored, in addition to conducting <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-going</span> due diligence, as described below. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Microsoft Due Diligence Policies and Practices </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft has articulated our human rights commitments and due diligence processes and provided ongoing public reporting on human rights (see <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/humanrights</span>). We have also made a public commitment to the Trusted Cloud Principles, which require us to respect internationally recognized rule of law and human rights standards. Finally, we have published an explanation of our approach to Operating Datacenters in Countries or Regions with Human Rights Challenges (see <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/datacenters_humanrights</span>) to provide transparency on our human rights related review processes for data center siting and operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft works to operate responsibly and in accordance with our global commitment to respect human rights and the rule of law. Microsoft&#8217;s approach is not limited to any particular country or project. We apply a global, risk-based due diligence framework to evaluate potential human rights impacts associated with our cloud operations and infrastructure investments, including in jurisdictions that present heightened human rights, governance, security, or geopolitical risks. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">In particular, when considering expansion of our data center footprint to new countries, we are guided by the commitments found in our Global Human Rights Statement (see <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/humanrights</span>), which include that we conduct human rights due diligence in line with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights. That due diligence is global and ongoing, and includes corporate-wide assessments, supply chain due diligence, and market-specific reviews. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">To inform responsible market entry, including datacenter siting, we conduct extensive reviews, which include public assessment materials from trusted, independent third-party resources, including Freedom House reports, the World Justice Project Rule of Law Index, and the Transparency International Corruption Perceptions Index. We also regularly source additional input from outside counsel and other experts with international expertise in privacy and other human rights-related matters. Through collaboration from teams across the Company, we aim to develop a thorough and nuanced understanding of the applicable market and jurisdiction, including the potential risks to human rights. </p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As appropriate, in certain geographies, we also conduct heightened due diligence via country-level human rights impact assessments that surface potential human rights risks, including risks to privacy, freedom of expression, and government access to data, as well as other risks associated with data center siting and operation, and identify potential mitigations to minimize those risks. We use what we learn from these studies to inform decision-making, develop and refine our policies and practices, mitigate risks, and improve our technologies and how we provide them to fulfill our commitment to human rights. We update these analyses as conditions and/or our engagement in the geography changes. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Beyond &#8220;go/no go&#8221; decisions, Microsoft also implements datacenter risk mitigation measures that typically take any or all of three forms: restrictions on specific types of services (e.g., not offering consumer services that collect personal data), technologies (e.g., not offering facial recognition technology), and/or specific types of customers (e.g., limiting access to higher risk customers). For example, in certain locations, we serve only enterprise customers and do not store consumer data to mitigate potential risks to the right to privacy and security, or we store data outside of the jurisdiction, rather than on site. Furthermore, all uses of Microsoft online services must comply with the Microsoft Services Agreement Code of Conduct (see <span style="text-decoration:underline">aka.ms/servicesconduct</span>), which prohibits use of our services to violate the rights of others, among other restrictions, and we have the right to suspend users for violations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Among those key risks are requirements that Microsoft comply with legally binding government demands for customer data and requirements to restrict publication of certain content in jurisdictions where we locate data centers. Our commitment to the rule of law carries with it an obligation to comply with applicable local law. When we receive a government request for customer data or to remove content, we assess whether it is valid, legally binding, and consistent with applicable law and with international norms on human rights and the rule of law, and we report on the requests we receive country by country, as described below. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">For example, Microsoft followed these processes in evaluating the establishment of a new cloud datacenter region in Saudi Arabia and in determining it could be operated in a way consistent with Microsoft&#8217;s commitment to respecting fundamental rights and focus on responsible cloud practices. Microsoft engaged an independent third party with expertise in human rights to support this review. Through a combination of research and stakeholder engagement with leading human rights experts, globally and regionally, the assessment team identified a range of salient human rights risks for Microsoft&#8217;s consideration. The assessment concluded with a series of potential risk mitigation actions. The mitigation actions identified fall within the categories described above: limits on the services and technologies we offer, limits on the customers we serve, and controls on where customer data is stored, in addition to <span style="white-space:nowrap">on-going</span> deal and other due diligence consistent with our approach globally. Consistent with our practice of updating these analyses as conditions change, we periodically refresh this assessment. Our approach and process are consistent globally, including in the jurisdictions mentioned in the proposal. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Trusted Cloud Principles </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Customer and technical demand for more cloud computing infrastructure will continue to grow, including in underserved regions not currently equipped with modern IT infrastructure, and Microsoft is not the only provider of such services. When expanding into these regions, it is critical for competing providers to avoid a race to the bottom by maintaining a consistent approach grounded in international best practices. That is why we worked with other major cloud service providers to develop, agree to, and publish the Trusted Cloud Principles. With these principles, Microsoft and other leading cloud computing services companies publicly commit to: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Arial; font-size:9pt;border-spacing:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

As part of our datacenter expansion in new countries, we review and assess these laws and policies prior to any expansion, and where necessary, we have successfully negotiated with Governments to establish processes and conditions, grounded in our principles, under which we will review law enforcement requests for data. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Engagement with independent experts and assessments </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We regularly consult independent human rights experts and participate in multistakeholder initiatives, which bring outside perspective to our due diligence and help us identify where to improve. Our corporate saliency assessment, repeated at regular intervals and conducted by independent business and human rights experts, provides a complete enterprise review of our practices. </p>

<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; border-top:6.00pt solid #0075c9">&#160;</p></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">
We participate in regulatory reporting that requires disclosure of our risk management and due diligence frameworks. Microsoft also undertakes voluntary assessments, such as our regular Global Network Initiative (&#8220;GNI&#8221;) Assessment, which involves a review by an accredited independent assessor to evaluate whether Microsoft is making a good faith effort to implement the GNI Principles on freedom of expression and privacy, with improvement over time. GNI publishes public assessment reports on its website. </p> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Additional Microsoft Transparency and Reporting </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">For more than a decade, twice a year Microsoft publishes the number of legal demands for customer data that we receive from governments (including law enforcement, national security, and civil authorities) around the world. The reports are broken out <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">country-by-country</span></span> and provide granular data and percentages of government requests received, cases where we disclosed customer content, cases where we disclosed only subscriber/transactional data, cases where no data was found, and cases where Microsoft rejected requests for not meeting legal requirements. The reports detail Microsoft&#8217;s principles and policies for ensuring that Microsoft handles government requests in ways that meet our commitments to uphold customer privacy standards across jurisdictions. We provide similarly detailed twice annual reporting on how Microsoft responds to government requests to remove published content. These and related reports are available in the Digital Trust Reports section of <span style="text-decoration:underline">microsoft.com/transparency</span>, which also provides detailed FAQs on our policies and practices for responding to government requests. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We recognize that decisions on where and how we operate and provide our technologies can have significant impact on human rights. As we pursue our mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more, we will continue to conduct due diligence to assess the impact of our technologies on human rights, engage and learn from stakeholders, and model responsible business practices and respect for human rights. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The proposal does not identify specific information necessary for shareholders to evaluate Company performance that is not already available through Microsoft&#8217;s existing disclosures. Rather, it requests another report covering processes, governance mechanisms, and risk-management approaches that Microsoft already describes publicly. </p> <p style="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:12pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">Proposal&#160;7:&#160;Board Chair and CEO Separation </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The New York State Common Retirement Fund has advised us that they intend to submit the following proposal for consideration at the Annual Meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Resolved:</span> Shareholders request the Board of Directors of Microsoft Corporation adopt a policy, and amend the governing documents as necessary, to require that two separate people hold the office of Chairman of the Board and the office of Chief Executive Officer as follows:</p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Selection of the Chair: The Board requires the separation of the offices of the Chair and the CEO. Whenever possible, the Chair shall be an Independent Director, as defined by the Director Independence Guidelines. The Board may select a temporary Chair who is not an Independent Director to serve while the Board seeks an Independent Chair. The Chair should not be a former CEO of the company. Selection of the Chair shall be consistent with applicable law and existing contracts.</p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="font-weight:bold">Supporting Statement:</span> The Board Chair and CEO roles, while often requiring similar skills, ultimately have differing responsibilities that are each key to the success of the Company. The CEO is responsible for the general charge and supervision of the business of the Corporation, while the Chair is designed to lead the Board of Directors in overseeing the Company&#8217;s integrity, risk management, succession planning, and CEO evaluation. One individual holding both offices diminishes the effectiveness of each role and compromises the Board&#8217;s responsibility for executive oversight.</p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The presence of a combined <span style="white-space:nowrap">Chair-CEO</span> on the Board can have a chilling effect on independent Board members&#8217; willingness to push back on management decisions. According to the CFA Institute&#8217;s Research and Policy Center, combining the positions can cause executive directors to have undue influence on the Board&#8217;s decision-making process and impair the willingness of other directors to exercise independent judgment. A combined <span style="white-space:nowrap">Chair-CEO</span> also leads the very body charged with evaluating the CEO&#8217;s performance and succession, creating an inherent conflict of interest.</p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft has benefited from an independent chairmanship before. Former Lead Independent Director John Thompson served as the Board&#8217;s independent Chairman from February 2014 to June 2021 and presided over a period of significant growth for the Company while working alongside CEO Nadella. Recombining the roles in 2021 reversed a structure the Board itself deliberately chose.</p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The need for independent Board leadership is heightened by Microsoft&#8217;s generational capital commitments to AI and data center infrastructure, alongside workforce reductions in 2024 and 2025, and other labor controversies. Furthermore, this rapid data center expansion has triggered escalating regulatory, community, and public scrutiny regarding its massive power consumption and environmental impact.</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">An increasing number of companies and investors see the benefits of a separate Chair and CEO structure. In 2025, 42&#160;percent of S&amp;P 500 Index company boards were chaired by an independent director, compared to 29&#160;percent in 2015.</p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">We urge Microsoft shareholders to support this proposal.</p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold">Board Recommendation </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">The Board of Directors recommends a vote AGAINST the proposal for the following reasons: </span></span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial;font-weight:bold">COMPANY STATEMENT IN OPPOSITION </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board of Directors believes this proposal to require that two separate people hold the office of Chairman of the Board and the office of Chief Executive Officer is not in the best interest of Microsoft&#8217;s shareholders. In the Board&#8217;s opinion, it is important for the Board to retain discretion to determine the most effective leadership structure, ensuring the exercise of fiduciary judgment and the ability to respond to the Company&#8217;s evolving needs and shareholder interests. If the Company were to adopt a policy that required to Company to have an independent chair, that policy could unnecessarily and detrimentally restrict the Board&#8217;s ability to determine the leadership structure that best serves shareholders and could prevent the Board from selecting the individual it believes is most qualified to serve as Chair based on the company&#8217;s circumstances at a particular time. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As the needs of the business evolve, the Board believes it is important to maintain flexibility to determine the leadership structure best suited to serving the interests of the Company and its shareholders at any given time. Accordingly, the Microsoft Corporate Governance Guidelines state: &#8220;To ensure robust independent leadership on the Board, if the individual appointed as Chair is not an independent director, or when the independent directors determine that it is in the best interests of the Company, the independent directors will also annually appoint a Lead Independent Director.&#8221; The Board&#8217;s independent directors annually appoint a Chairman, considering the Company&#8217;s evolving needs, strategic priorities, and the unique skills of its leaders. Consistent with the Board&#8217;s belief in the importance of flexibility, there is no fixed policy as to whether the Chairman should be an independent director, an affiliated director, or a member of management. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The Board&#8217;s current structure, featuring a strong Lead Independent Director and robust corporate governance practices, provides effective oversight, accountability, and alignment with the interests of long-term shareholders. The Board&#8217;s leadership structure allocates authority, responsibility, and oversight between management and the independent members of the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Currently, the Board believes that our CEO is the director best qualified to serve as Chair given his extensive knowledge of the company&#8217;s business, strategy, opportunities, and risks. For that reason, the independent directors have Satya Nadella as Chairman, leveraging his deep understanding of Microsoft&#8217;s business and technology platform, AI strategy, and global competitive landscape to elevate strategic opportunities and identify key risks for Board review. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">As contemplated by the Corporate Governance Guidelines, when Mr.&#160;Nadella was appointed Chairman, the Board also appointed a Lead Independent Director. The Lead Independent Director at Microsoft is empowered with significant authority and responsibilities to ensure that: the Board&#8217;s independent oversight of management is robust, promotes effective communication between management and Directors, and supports consideration of key governance matters. As is described in the Board Leadership section of this proxy, Microsoft&#8217;s Lead Independent Director&#8217;s key responsibilities and authority include: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.86em; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial"><span style="color:#0075c9">PROPOSALS&#160;TO<br/>BE&#160;VOTED&#160;ON&#160;DURING<br/>THE MEETING</span></p></td>

<td style="vertical-align:top"> <p style="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.86em; font-size:7pt; font-family:Arial">INFORMATION&#8195;&#8195;&#8195;<br/>ABOUT THE<br/>MEETING</p></td></tr>

<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom"/></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="width:97%; margin-top:1.5%; margin-bottom:1.5%; margin-left:1.5%; margin-right:-1.25%">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Sandra Peterson currently serves as Lead Independent Director. In this role, Ms.&#160;Peterson has focused on recruiting and leading a highly qualified and independent Board, including overseeing long-term director succession and Board education efforts to ensure the Board&#8217;s skills and experience continue to align with Microsoft&#8217;s evolving strategic direction. She has broadened the Board&#8217;s engagement with leaders across Microsoft&#8217;s businesses and enhanced oversight of key strategic matters, including AI transformation, security, quality, capital allocation and deployment, and long-term growth. In addition, she directs the Board&#8217;s independent evaluation of CEO performance and plays a key role in executive succession planning. In consultation with the CEO, Vice Chair, and other directors, Ms.&#160;Peterson shapes the Board&#8217;s agenda and priorities and has final approval authority over Board meeting schedules and agendas. Throughout her tenure, she has proactively engaged with Microsoft&#8217;s shareholders to gather perspectives on governance practices, Board effectiveness, and other matters important to investors. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Microsoft maintains other leading corporate governance practices, including a majority-independent Board, fully independent key committees, annual director elections, Board and CEO performance evaluations, proxy access, and the right for shareholders to call special meetings. Consistent with their fiduciary duties under Washington state law, the Lead Independent Director and all independent directors are empowered to seek additional information from management as they deem appropriate. The Governance and Nominating Committee of the Board, comprised solely of independent directors, determines and recommends the slate of director nominees for election to the Board and recommends the composition of Board committees and committee chairs to the Board. The CEO is not a member of the Governance and Nominating Committee or any other committee and the Board and all Committees hold executive sessions without management present as a regular practice. These practices provide additional checks and balances to foster accountability. While some investors may favor an independent Chair model, there is no consensus that it produces superior governance or performance. Leading public companies use a range of structures, with effective oversight&#8212;not role separation&#8212;driving outcomes. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Finally, the proposal does not identify, and the Board does not believe there is, any governance deficiency, oversight failure, responsiveness concern, or performance concern that would be addressed by imposing a mandatory separation policy. Mr.&#160;Nadella was appointed CEO in February 2014 and Chairman in June 2021. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Mr.&#160;Nadella&#8217;s tenure as the combined CEO and Chairman has been marked by exceptional, sustained financial performance that has contributed to significant value creation for long-term shareholders. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">The current leadership structure of our Board and our existing corporate governance practices have served our shareholders well. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p></div>

It is furnished in connection with the solicitation of proxies by the Board of Directors of Microsoft Corporation to be voted during the Annual Meeting for the purposes set forth in the accompanying Notice of Annual Meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Arial">Shareholders who execute proxies retain the right to revoke them at any time before the shares are voted by proxy during the meeting.
